2.4.1.1: I bow to Śiva, whose mind is pleased by salutation, who holds intense love dear and bestows love; who is full and makes others full, the sole abode of all complete sovereign powers; who is Truth, made of truth, whose glory is true in the three times, who loves truth and grants truth; to Śaṅkara, praised by Viṣṇu and Brahmā, who has taken on a form out of his own grace. ॥1॥
2.4.1.2: Nārada said: After marrying Girijā, what did Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the worlds, do on going to his own mountain, O Brahmā? Tell me that. ॥2॥
2.4.1.3: How indeed was a son born to Śiva, the Supreme Self, for whose sake the Lord, though delighting in his own Self, married Śivā? ॥3॥
2.4.1.4: How, O Brahmā, did the slaying of Tāraka, which brought welfare to the gods, come about? Tell me all this completely, showing kindness to me. ॥4॥
2.4.1.5: Sūta said: Having heard these words of Nārada, Prajāpati, his mind well pleased, remembered Śaṅkara and replied. ॥5॥
2.4.1.6: Brahmā said: Listen, O Nārada: I shall tell the deeds of the moon-crested one, the divine story of Guha's birth and the righteous slaying of the demon Tāraka. ॥6॥
2.4.1.7: Let it be heard: today I narrate a story that destroys sin, hearing which a person is surely freed from all sins. ॥7॥
2.4.1.8: This narrative is pure, secret and supremely wonderful; it removes the torment of sin and destroys all obstacles. ॥8॥
2.4.1.9: It grants every auspiciousness, is the essence, delightful to all ears, gives happiness, is the seed of liberation, and cuts the root of karma. ॥9॥
2.4.1.10: Having come to Kailāsa after marrying Śivā, Śiva too attained great splendour; and he reflected on the task of the gods, and also on the suffering of people in carrying out the gods' task. ॥10॥
2.4.1.11: When that Lord Śiva himself went to Kailāsa, all the Gaṇas, overjoyed, made various festivities. ॥11॥
2.4.1.12: When Śiva had come to Kailāsa there was a great festival; the gods returned to their own domains, their minds brimming with joy. ॥12॥
2.4.1.13: Then Śambhu, the Great God, taking Girijā, Śivā, went to a solitary place, most divine and charming. ॥13॥
2.4.1.14: There he made a bed conducive to love, strewn with flowers and sandal paste, wonderful, supreme, auspicious, and furnished with articles of enjoyment. ॥14॥
2.4.1.15: There the Lord Śambhu, the giver of honour, sported with Girijā for a thousand years by the reckoning of the gods. ॥15॥
2.4.1.16: By the mere touch of Durgā's body Śiva playfully swooned; and she, swooning from Śiva's touch, did not know day from night. ॥16॥
2.4.1.17: While Hara was engaged in enjoyment, setting in motion the way of the world, a great span of time passed for the two of them like a moment, O sinless one. ॥17॥
2.4.1.18: Then once, dear son, all the gods led by Śakra gathered together, came to Meru and held counsel. ॥18॥
2.4.1.19: The gods said: The Lord Śambhu, lord of yogins, changeless, delighting in his own Self, stainless, married for the sake of our task. ॥19॥
2.4.1.20: No son has been born to him; we do not know the reason for this. Why is this delay being made by the lord of the gods? ॥20॥
2.4.1.21: Brahmā said: Meanwhile the gods learned from Nārada, who sees the divine, the extent of the enjoyment of the two as they made love. ॥21॥
2.4.1.22: Knowing the enjoyment of the two to be long-lasting, those gods became anxious and, putting me, Brahmā, at their head, went to Nārāyaṇa. ॥22॥
2.4.1.23: Bowing to him, I related the whole matter as desired; all the gods stood still like figures in a painting. ॥23॥
2.4.1.24: I said: For a thousand years by the gods' reckoning Śaṅkara, absorbed in love-play and motionless, the yogin, does not desist. ॥24॥
2.4.1.25: The Lord said: There is no cause for worry, O creator of the world; all will be well. O lord of gods, go for refuge to Śaṅkara, the great Lord. ॥25॥
2.4.1.26: Those people who with their mind and with joy have taken refuge in Maheśa — for those devotees, O lord of creatures, there is no fear from anywhere at any time. ॥26॥
2.4.1.27: The interruption of their love-play will happen in due time, not now, O Vidhi. A task prompted by time attains success, not otherwise. ॥27॥
2.4.1.28: Who here is able to break off Śambhu's cherished love-union? When a thousand years are complete, he will desist of his own accord. ॥28॥
2.4.1.29: Whoever by some device breaks off the love-making of a woman and a man suffers separation from wife and sons birth after birth. ॥29॥
2.4.1.30: Here he becomes bereft of knowledge, his fame lost, deprived of fortune; and at the end that sinner goes to the Kālasūtra hell for a hundred thousand years. ॥30॥
2.4.1.31: The great lord of sages Durvāsas made this Śakra, united with Rambhā, desist from love-play; as a result, his separation from his wife came about. ॥31॥
2.4.1.32: Again, having obtained and enjoyed another, fair-handed woman, after a thousand divine years he cast off the fever of separation. ॥32॥
2.4.1.33: Guru Bṛhaspati restrained Kāma while he was embracing Ghṛtācī; within six months Candra carried off his wife. ॥33॥
2.4.1.34: Then, having worshipped Śiva and fought the war over Tārā, he got Tārā back, pregnant, and cast off the fever of separation. ॥34॥
2.4.1.35: The great seer Gautama made Candra, who was with Mohinī, desist from love-play; as a result, his separation from his wife came about. ॥35॥
2.4.1.36: Hariścandra stopped a ploughman who lay motionless, united with a low-caste woman in a lonely place; hear the result of that. ॥36॥
2.4.1.37: He was deprived of wife, son and kingdom and was tormented by Viśvāmitra; then, having worshipped Śiva, he was freed from that misery. ॥37॥
2.4.1.38: Out of fear, the gods did not restrain Ajāmila, the best of brahmins, when he was united with a low-caste woman, nor did anyone restrain her. ॥38॥
2.4.1.39: Everything is accomplished through destiny (niṣeka), O Vidhi; destiny is powerful. It indeed gives its fruit; by whom can destiny be warded off? ॥39॥
2.4.1.40: That love-making of Śambhu lasts a thousand divine years; when the thousand years are complete, O lords of gods, go there… ॥40॥
2.4.1.41: You will certainly do that by which the semen falls upon the ground. And from that semen will be born the Lord's son, named Skanda. ॥41॥
2.4.1.42: Now go to your own abode, O Vidhi, together with the hosts of gods. Let Śambhu enjoy union with Pārvatī in solitude. ॥42॥
2.4.1.43: Brahmā said: Having said this, the beloved of Kamalā quickly went to his own inner palace. The gods, along with me, went to their own abodes, O lord of sages. ॥43॥
2.4.1.44: Then, through the intense love-play of Śakti and the Possessor of Śakti, the earth, overwhelmed by the weight, trembled, together with Śeṣa and the Tortoise. ॥44॥
2.4.1.45: Indeed, through the weight on the Tortoise, the wind, the support of all, was brought to a standstill; then the three worlds became distraught with fear. ॥45॥
2.4.1.46: Then all the gods, with me, went to Hari for refuge and, dejected in mind, reported that whole occurrence. ॥46॥
2.4.1.47: The gods said: O God of gods, Lord of Ramā, O Master who protects all, save us who have come to you for refuge, our minds agitated by fear. ॥47॥
2.4.1.48: The life-breath of the three worlds has been stilled, for what reason we do not know. The three worlds, with moving and unmoving beings, together with the sages and gods, are in distress. ॥48॥
2.4.1.49: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, all the gods, with me, O lord of sages, stood dejected before Viṣṇu, fallen silent and deeply grieved. ॥49॥
2.4.1.50: Hearing that, Hari took all of us gods with him and quickly went to Mount Kailāsa, dear to Śiva. ॥50॥
2.4.1.51: Having gone there, Hari, dear to the gods, together with the gods and me, went to Śiva's excellent abode, desiring to see Śaṅkara. ॥51॥
2.4.1.52: Not seeing Śiva there, Viṣṇu along with the gods was astonished. Full of humility, he questioned Śiva's attendants (gaṇas) stationed there. ॥52॥
2.4.1.53: Viṣṇu said: O followers of Śaṅkara, O gaṇas, where has Śiva, the Lord of all, gone? Kindly tell us, who are distressed, O compassionate ones. ॥53॥
2.4.1.54: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of Hari, who was accompanied by the gods, those gaṇas of Śaṅkara spoke affectionately to the Lord of Ramā. ॥54॥
2.4.1.55: The attendants of Śiva said: O Hari, listen: out of love for Śiva we shall truly tell you, together with Brahmā and the gods, the whole account as it happened. ॥55॥
2.4.1.56: Mahādeva, the Lord of all, adept in many kinds of divine play, went to Girijā's dwelling, having lovingly stationed us here. ॥56॥
2.4.1.57: What Śambhu, the great Lord, is doing inside that cave we do not know, O Lord of Ramā; many years have passed. ॥57॥
2.4.1.58: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of theirs, that Viṣṇu, with the gods and me, greatly astonished, O best of sages, went to Śiva's door. ॥58॥
2.4.1.59: Having gone there with me and the gods, that Hari, dear to the gods, then called out in an anguished voice, in a loud tone, O sage. ॥59॥
2.4.1.60: Standing there, O best of sages, Hari, together with the gods and me, praised Śambhu with great love—Hara, Lord of all the worlds. ॥60॥
2.4.1.61: Viṣṇu said: What are you doing within, O Mahādeva, Supreme Lord? Protect all of us gods, tormented by Tāraka, who have come to you for refuge. ॥61॥
2.4.1.62: Praising Śambhu thus in many ways, Hari, together with me and the gods tormented by Tāraka, wept bitterly there, O lord of sages. ॥62॥
2.4.1.63: There arose there a tumult of grief from the heaven-dwellers, the afflicted gods, mingled with praise of Śiva, O lord of sages. ॥63॥
2.4.1.iti: Thus ends the first adhyāya, named Śiva's sport, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥1॥
2.4.2.1: Brahmā said: Having heard that, Mahādeva, expert in yoga and knowledge, though he had given up desire, did not break off his union with her for fear of Pārvatī. ॥1॥
2.4.2.2: Śiva came to the door of the house, near the gods who were oppressed by the demon — Śaṅkara, who is affectionate to his devotees. ॥2॥
2.4.2.3: Then all the gods, together with Hari and me, having seen the Lord Śiva, affectionate to devotees, became exceedingly happy. ॥3॥
2.4.2.4: Having thus heard the words of those gods, the blessed Bhava replied, dejected in spirit, with an aching heart. ॥4॥
2.4.2.5: Bowing with very great love, their shoulders bent, all the immortals, together with me and Hari, praised Śaṅkara, O sage. ॥5॥
2.4.2.6: The gods said: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, O ocean of compassion, O Lord, you are indeed the inner controller of all; you know everything, O Śaṅkara. ॥6॥
2.4.2.7: Accomplish the gods' task, O all-pervading one; protect the gods, O Maheśvara. Showing compassion, slay the demons headed by Tāraka, O great Lord. ॥7॥
2.4.2.8: Śiva said: O Viṣṇu, O Vidhi (Brahmā), O gods — the intent of all of you is known to me. What is to be, that indeed comes to pass; no one can prevent it. ॥8॥
2.4.2.9: What has happened has happened. Listen to the matter at hand, O immortals: who will now take my semen that has slipped forth from Śiva? ॥9॥
2.4.2.10: Saying, let him take it, he let it fall upon the ground. Then Agni, having become a dove, urged on by all the gods, ॥10॥
2.4.2.11: then swallowed the whole of Śambhu's semen with his beak. Meanwhile, O sage, Girijā came there. ॥11॥
2.4.2.12: And as Śiva's return was delayed, she saw the foremost of the gods; having learned that whole affair, Śivā was filled with great wrath. ॥12॥
2.4.2.13: Then she spoke to all the gods, headed by Hari. ॥13॥
2.4.2.14: The Goddess said: O you hosts of gods, all of you are especially wicked. Ever bent on achieving your own ends, you cause suffering to others for that purpose. ॥14॥
2.4.2.15: For your own sake you propitiated Maheśāna, the supreme Lord, and spoiled my love-sport; I have become barren, O gods. ॥15॥
2.4.2.16: By opposing me, O immortals, no one at all finds happiness; therefore suffering shall indeed befall you, wicked dwellers of heaven. ॥16॥
2.4.2.17: Brahmā said: Having said this, Śivā, the daughter of the king of mountains, blazing with fury, cursed all the gods headed by Viṣṇu. ॥17॥
2.4.2.18: Pārvatī said: From this day on, may the wives of the gods be barren; and may all the gods who oppose me be miserable. ॥18॥
2.4.2.19: Brahmā said: Having thus cursed all the gods headed by Viṣṇu, the Mistress of all, enraged, spoke to Pāvaka (Agni), the swallower of Śiva's semen. ॥19॥
2.4.2.20: Pārvatī said: Be an eater of everything, O Śuci, and ever tormented in yourself. You do not know the truth of Śiva; you are a fool, a mere doer of the gods' business. ॥20॥
2.4.2.21: O rogue, most wicked one, of wicked mind even among the wicked, in swallowing Śiva's semen you did not do what was proper and beneficial. ॥21॥
2.4.2.22: Brahmā said: Having thus cursed Fire, Śivā, the mountain's daughter, still dissatisfied, quickly went from there to her own abode with the Lord, O sage. ॥22॥
2.4.2.23: Having gone there, Śivā carefully and fully made Śiva understand, and she brought forth an excellent son named Gaṇeśa, O lord of sages. ॥23॥
2.4.2.24: I shall describe that whole account later, O sage. Now listen with great delight: I tell of the birth of Guha. ॥24॥
2.4.2.25: The immortals indeed eat the food and other offerings placed in the fire — so says the word of the Veda; hence all those gods became pregnant. ॥25॥
2.4.2.26: Then, unable to bear that semen, all the gods headed by Viṣṇu became greatly afflicted, their minds ruined by Śivā's command. ॥26॥
2.4.2.27: Then all the gods headed by Viṣṇu, bewildered and burning, quickly went for refuge to the Lord of Pārvatī. ॥27॥
2.4.2.28: Going to the door of Śiva's abode, all the gods, humbled, with joined palms, lovingly praised Śambhu together with Śivā. ॥28॥
2.4.2.29: The gods said: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, O Lord of Girijā, O great Lord, what has now happened, O master? Your māyā is hard to overcome. ॥29॥
2.4.2.30: We have become pregnant and are burning with your semen, O Śambhu. Show compassion; remove this condition. ॥30॥
2.4.2.31: Brahmā said: Having heard this praise of the immortals, the supreme Lord, husband of Śivā, swiftly came to the door where the gods stood, O sage. ॥31॥
2.4.2.32: All the gods together with Acyuta, bowing to Śaṅkara, affectionate to devotees, who had come to the door, lovingly praised him, dancing with joy. ॥32॥
2.4.2.33: The gods said: O Śambhu, O Śiva, O Maheśāna, we bow to you especially. Protect us, who have come for refuge and are burning with the semen. ॥33॥
2.4.2.34: Remove this suffering, O Hara. Surely we are dying. Without you, who today is able to remove the gods' suffering? ॥34॥
2.4.2.35: Brahmā said: Having heard these most piteous words, the Lord, king of the gods, affectionate to devotees, laughed and then replied to the gods. ॥35॥
2.4.2.36: Śiva said: O Hari, O Vidhi, O gods, all of you listen to my words: today you will have relief; be attentive. ॥36॥
2.4.2.37: All you gods, vomit out this semen of mine at once; by the command of me, your good Lord, you will then be especially happy. ॥37॥
2.4.2.38: Brahmā said: Placing this command on their heads, all the gods headed by Viṣṇu quickly vomited, remembering the imperishable Śiva. ॥38॥
2.4.2.39: That semen of Śambhu, gold-like in hue, wondrous, the shape of a mountain, fell upon the earth, very radiant, touching the very sky. ॥39॥
2.4.2.40: All the gods, Acyuta (Viṣṇu) and the rest, became happy, and they praised the supreme Lord Śaṅkara, who is affectionate to his devotees. ॥40॥
2.4.2.41: But Pāvaka (Agni) alone did not become happy there, O lord of sages. Śaṅkara, the supreme Lord, then gave him a command. ॥41॥
2.4.2.42: Then that Fire-god, distressed, with joined palms and bowing low, O sage, praised Śiva, not at ease in himself, and spoke these words. ॥42॥
2.4.2.43: Agni said: O God of gods, O great Lord, I, your servant, am a fool. Forgive my offence and remove my burning. ॥43॥
2.4.2.44: You, O master, are kind to the afflicted; you are Śaṅkara, the supreme Lord. Thus Pāvaka, with a gracious mind, replied to the one who is kind to the afflicted. ॥44॥
2.4.2.45: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of Śuci (Agni), that Śambhu, the supreme Lord, kind to the afflicted, replied to Pāvaka with a gracious mind. ॥45॥
2.4.2.46: Śiva said: You did an improper deed in that you swallowed my semen. Hence the burning came from the excess of sin; now by my command your burning has ceased. ॥46॥
2.4.2.47: Now, O Śuci, you have truly become happy, since you have sought refuge in me. Therefore I have become pleased; all your sorrow is perishing. ॥47॥
2.4.2.48: Carefully deposit my semen in the womb of some good woman; then you will become happy and especially free from burning. ॥48॥
2.4.2.49: Brahmā said: Having heard these words of Śambhu, Śuci, with joined palms and bowing, replied slowly and with affection to Śaṅkara, the benefactor of devotees. ॥49॥
2.4.2.50: O Lord, O Maheśvara, this energy of yours is unapproachable. Apart from Śakti, there is no woman in the three worlds able to hold it in her womb. ॥50॥
2.4.2.51: When the Fire-god spoke thus, then you, O best of sages, prompted by Śaṅkara and wishing to help, spoke to Agni with sincere heart. ॥51॥
2.4.2.52: Nārada said: Listen, O Fire, to my auspicious words which will take away your burning, which grant supreme bliss, are pleasing, and remove all distress. ॥52॥
2.4.2.53: Having carried out this remedy, O Fire, be happy and free of burning. By Śiva's will I have properly told you this with respect, dear one. ॥53॥
2.4.2.54: O Śuci, those women who perform the early-morning bath in the month of Tapas (Māgha) — in their bodies place this great semen of Śiva. ॥54॥
2.4.2.55: Brahmā said: At that moment the wives of the seven sages came there in the morning, observing their vows, wishing to bathe in the month of Tapas, O sage. ॥55॥
2.4.2.56: Having bathed, six of those women, afflicted by severe cold and wishing to leave, went near the flames of the fire, O sage. ॥56॥
2.4.2.57: Seeing them deluded by Giriśa's command, Arundhatī, of virtuous conduct and good understanding, firmly forbade them. ॥57॥
2.4.2.58: Those six sages' wives, deluded by Śiva's Māyā, went there forcibly out of infatuation, O sage, to rid themselves of their cold. ॥58॥
2.4.2.59: At once the particles of that semen entered their bodies, all of them through the pores of the hair, O sage, and the Fire-god became free of burning. ॥59॥
2.4.2.60: Vanishing quickly, the Fire-god in the form of flame went happily to his own world, remembering you and that Śaṅkara in his mind. ॥60॥
2.4.2.61: Those women, O virtuous one, became pregnant and were tormented by burning; they went to their own homes, dear one. Arundhatī was grieved on account of Agni. ॥61॥
2.4.2.62: Seeing the condition of their wives, dear one, the husbands, overcome with anger, quickly abandoned those women after consulting together, dear one. ॥62॥
2.4.2.63: Then all those six women, seeing their apparent unfaithfulness, were filled with great sorrow, dear one, and became troubled in mind. ॥63॥
2.4.2.64: The sages' wives cast off that semen of Śiva in the form of an embryo on the ridge of the Himālaya, and then became free of burning. ॥64॥
2.4.2.65: Unable to bear that semen of Śiva, the Himālaya began to tremble and, tormented by the burning, quickly threw the unbearable substance into the Gaṅgā. ॥65॥
2.4.2.66: And by the Gaṅgā too that unbearable seed of the Supreme Self was cast by her own waves into a clump of reeds, O lord of sages. ॥66॥
2.4.2.67: That semen, having fallen there, quickly became a boy — handsome, charming, glorious, radiant, increasing delight. ॥67॥
2.4.2.68: In the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, in the bright fortnight, on the sixth lunar day, O lord of sages, the manifestation of that son of Śiva took place on earth. ॥68॥
2.4.2.69: At that moment, O Brahman, the daughter of the snowy mountain (Pārvatī) and Giriśa too suddenly became joyful there on their own mountain. ॥69॥
2.4.2.70: Milk born of joy flowed from Śivā's breasts; and, having gone there, everyone felt great happiness, O sage. ॥70॥
2.4.2.71: Auspiciousness arose in the three worlds, dear one, bringing happiness to the good; for the wicked, and especially for the Daityas, obstacles arose. ॥71॥
2.4.2.72: Suddenly a great sound of kettledrums arose in the sky, and a shower of flowers quickly fell upon the boy, O Nārada. ॥72॥
2.4.2.73: For all the gods, Viṣṇu and the rest, O best of sages, there suddenly arose supreme joy and a great festival. ॥73॥
2.4.2.iti: Thus ends the second adhyāya, named The birth of Śiva's son, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥2॥
2.4.3.1: Nārada said: O god of gods, lord of creatures, O Brahmā, maker of creation, O lord, what happened there after that? Be gracious and tell me that now. ॥1॥
2.4.3.2: Brahmā said: At that time, dear son, the mighty Viśvāmitra, prompted by the Creator, came there by chance, pleased at heart. ॥2॥
2.4.3.3: Seeing the unearthly radiance of that very brilliant son, he had his desires fulfilled; deeply delighted, he bowed down. ॥3॥
2.4.3.4: With a delighted mind, and with words inspired by the Creator, Viśvāmitra, who knew the boy's power, offered him fine praise. ॥4॥
2.4.3.5: Then the son there, the doer of great sports, became very pleased; laughing heartily, he of wondrous splendour spoke to Viśvāmitra. ॥5॥
2.4.3.6: The son of Śiva said: O greatly wise one, by Śiva's will you have come here unexpectedly. Dear sir, perform my purificatory rite properly, in accordance with the Veda. ॥6॥
2.4.3.7: From today on, be my priest, bringing me delight. You will always be worthy of worship by all; there is no doubt of this. ॥7॥
2.4.3.8: Brahmā said: Hearing his words, the son of Gādhi was greatly pleased, and, much astonished, he replied to him in a low voice. ॥8॥
2.4.3.9: Viśvāmitra said: Listen, dear child: I am not a brāhmaṇa. I am the kṣatriya son of Gādhi, known as Viśvāmitra, a kṣatriya who serves brāhmaṇas. ॥9॥
2.4.3.10: Thus I have told you my own story, O excellent boy. Who are you? Tell me your whole story, for I am astonished. ॥10॥
2.4.3.11: Brahmā said: Hearing his words, the boy told him his own story. Then the doer of great sports spoke with great affection to that son of Gādhi. ॥11॥
2.4.3.12: The son of Śiva said: O Viśvāmitra, by my boon you are a brahmarṣi; there is no doubt of this. Vasiṣṭha and the others will always praise you with respect. ॥12॥
2.4.3.13: Therefore, at my command, you should perform the rite. All this is to be kept strictly secret by you; it must not be told anywhere. ॥13॥
2.4.3.14: Brahmā said: Then, O divine sage, he lovingly performed for Śiva's son the complete rite, in the proper way, by the excellent procedure prescribed in the Veda. ॥14॥
2.4.3.15: Śiva's child too, the lord who performs great sports, greatly pleased, gave supreme divine knowledge to the sage Viśvāmitra. ॥15॥
2.4.3.16: The son of Śuci Agni made Viśvāmitra his priest; from then on Viśvāmitra was the best of the twice-born, and the boy remained skilled in manifold sports. ॥16॥
2.4.3.17: Thus was a sport performed by him, and I have narrated it, O sage. Now, dear son, listen with delight to another sport of his; I shall tell it. ॥17॥
2.4.3.18: At that time, dear son, the one named Śveta Agni then saw there his own divine, supremely purifying son. ॥18॥
2.4.3.19: Then Pāvaka Agni went to him, saw him, embraced and kissed him; calling him my son, he gave him a weapon — the Śakti spear. ॥19॥
2.4.3.20: Guha took that spear and climbed the peak; he struck it with that spear, and the peak fell to the ground. ॥20॥
2.4.3.21: Heroic rākṣasas numbering ten padmas, who had come earlier to kill him, were swiftly destroyed by that blow. ॥21॥
2.4.3.22: A great cry of alarm arose; the earth with its mountains quaked, and the three worlds too. The lord of the gods Indra, together with the gods, came there. ॥22॥
2.4.3.23: He struck him on his right side with the thunderbolt; from that was born a single very powerful man named Śākha. ॥23॥
2.4.3.24: Again Śakra quickly struck him then on the left side with the thunderbolt; another man was born, a second powerful one called Viśākha. ॥24॥
2.4.3.25: Then Śakra struck his heart with the thunderbolt; another man arose, called Naigama, likewise very powerful. ॥25॥
2.4.3.26: Then the four — Skanda and the others — great heroes of great strength, rushed swiftly to kill Indra; and he Indra sought his refuge. ॥26॥
2.4.3.27: Śakra, with the host of immortals, seized by fear, then left that place and went to his own world, bewildered; he did not understand the secret, O sage. ॥27॥
2.4.3.28: But that boy, the lord who performs manifold sports, remained right there, full of joy and fearless as before, dear son. ॥28॥
2.4.3.29: At that time six women called the Kṛttikās came there to bathe and saw that boy, the great lord. ॥29॥
2.4.3.30: All those Kṛttikā women set their minds on taking him; a quarrel arose among them, each eager to take him, O sage. ॥30॥
2.4.3.31: To settle their quarrel he made himself six faces and drank the milk of all of them; and they were satisfied, O sage. ॥31॥
2.4.3.32: Understanding the inclination of his mind, all those Kṛttikās then took him and joyfully went to their own world, O sage. ॥32॥
2.4.3.33: Giving the breast to him who longed for it, they raised that boy called Kumāra, the son of the Lord, more radiant than the sun. ॥33॥
2.4.3.34: They never let the boy out of their sight; dearer than life itself is a little son to the one who nurtures him. ॥34॥
2.4.3.35: Whatever garments were rare in the three worlds, those they lovingly gave him, and excellent ornaments too. ॥35॥
2.4.3.36: Day by day they nourished that boy, the great lord, feeding him especially with delicious, much-praised foods. ॥36॥
2.4.3.37: Then one day, dear son, that boy, the son of the Kṛttikās, went to the divine assembly of the gods and performed a fine feat. ॥37॥
2.4.3.38: The boy who performs great sports displayed his own most wondrous splendour to all the gods, Viṣṇu included. ॥38॥
2.4.3.39: Seeing him, all those gods, together with Acyuta and the sages, were utterly astonished and questioned the boy. ॥39॥
2.4.3.40: Who are you? Hearing that, he said nothing at all; he quickly went to his own abode and remained hidden as before. ॥40॥
2.4.3.iti: Thus ends the third adhyāya, named The sport of Kārttikeya, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥3॥
2.4.4.1: Nārada said: O god of gods, lord of creatures, O Vidhi (Brahmā), what happened then? Out of compassion, tell me now the account filled with Śiva's divine play. ॥1॥
2.4.4.2: Brahmā said: O sage, after that son of Śambhu had been taken by the Kṛttikās, some time passed, and the daughter of the Himālaya did not know of it. ॥2॥
2.4.4.3: At that time Durgā, her lotus-face smiling, spoke to her husband Śambhu, the Lord, the master of the gods of gods. ॥3॥
2.4.4.4: Pārvatī said: O god of gods, Mahādeva, hear my auspicious words. Through the great weight of my former merit I obtained you, the Lord as husband. ॥4॥
2.4.4.5: Out of grace, though the foremost among yogins, you became intent on amorous sport. There the interruption of my love-play was brought about by the gods and by you, O Bhava. ॥5॥
2.4.4.6: Your semen, O all-pervading one, fell on the ground, not into my womb. Where did it go, O god, and by which god was it concealed? ॥6॥
2.4.4.7: How could the unfailing semen of you, my lord, O Maheśvara, have become futile? Or what has happened? Has a child been born somewhere? ॥7॥
2.4.4.8: Brahmā said: Having heard Pārvatī's words, the Lord of the world laughed, summoned the gods and the sages too, and spoke, O lord of sages. ॥8॥
2.4.4.9: Maheśvara said: O gods, hear my words; Pārvatī's words have been heard. Where has my unfailing semen gone, and by whom was it concealed? ॥9॥
2.4.4.10: If the one who hid it, out of fear, does not quickly produce it, does he not deserve punishment? A king who, though able, is not a punisher of wrongdoers is a devourer of his people and deserves to be harassed by his subjects. ॥10॥
2.4.4.11: Brahmā said: Having heard those words of Śambhu and conferred among themselves, all of them, frightened, spoke one after another in the presence of the Lord. ॥11॥
2.4.4.12: Viṣṇu said: May those by whom your semen was concealed become, in Bhārata, liars, violators of the teacher's wife, ever devoted to reviling the teacher. ॥12॥
2.4.4.13: Brahmā said: He by whom your semen was concealed—may he never be blessed, there in the holy land of Bhārata, with your service and worship. ॥13॥
2.4.4.14: The guardians of the worlds said: The sinner who, under the delusion that it had merely fallen, concealed your semen—may he be utterly the recipient of that sin, its torment and its karma, perpetually. ॥14॥
2.4.4.15: The gods said: The fool who makes a vow and does not bring it to completion—may he by whom your semen was concealed be a vessel of that sin. ॥15॥
2.4.4.16: The wives of the gods said: May she by whom your semen was concealed be like the woman who reviles her own husband, goes to another man, and is bereft of mother and kin. ॥16॥
2.4.4.17: Brahmā said: Having heard the words of the gods, Hara, lord of the gods of gods, spoke awe-inspiring words to Dharma and the others, the witnesses of all deeds. ॥17॥
2.4.4.18: Śrī Śiva said: It was not concealed by the gods; then by whom was that semen surely concealed—that unfailing semen of me, the blessed Maheśa, the Lord? ॥18॥
2.4.4.19: You are all constantly the witnesses of all deeds. What is hidden from you? Or rather, what you know, you ought to tell. ॥19॥
2.4.4.20: Brahmā said: Having heard the Lord's words, they trembled in the assembly; looking at one another, they spoke in turn before the Lord. ॥20॥
2.4.4.21: Brahmā said: When you rose from love-play, the semen fell onto the surface of the earth. I knew it to be unfailing, having fallen because of Śaṅkara's agitation. ॥21॥
2.4.4.22: The Earth said: Unable to bear the semen, I formerly cast it into Fire. Hence, O Brahman, since it was hard to bear here, you should forgive me, a weak woman. ॥22॥
2.4.4.23: Agni said: Unable to bear your semen, O Śaṅkara, I, in the form of a dove, at once cast that most unbearable semen on Mount Kailāsa. ॥23॥
2.4.4.24: The mountain said: Unable to bear your semen, O Śaṅkara, protector of the worlds, I at once cast that unbearable semen into the Gaṅgā, O supreme Lord. ॥24॥
2.4.4.25: Gaṅgā said: Unable to bear your semen, O Śaṅkara, protector of the worlds, greatly distressed, O Lord, O master, I cast it into the forest of reeds. ॥25॥
2.4.4.26: Vāyu said: The semen that fell among the reeds at once became a child, exceedingly beautiful, O Śambhu, on the holy bank of the heavenly river. ॥26॥
2.4.4.27: Sūrya said: Having seen the crying child, O Lord, I went to the western mountain of setting, impelled by the wheel of time, unable to remain at night. ॥27॥
2.4.4.28: Candra said: The band of Kṛttikās, going to Badarikāśrama, came upon the crying child, took him, and went to their own abode, O Śambhu. ॥28॥
2.4.4.29: The water said: Having brought him, crying, they nourished with their breast-milk your son, O Lord, son of the Īśa, radiant as the sun. ॥29॥
2.4.4.30: Sandhyā said: Now, having fostered that little son in the forest, the Kṛttikās lovingly, out of delight, gave him the name Kārttika. ॥30॥
2.4.4.31: The night said: They never let the boy out of their sight. To whoever nourishes him, a little son is an object of love dearer even than life. ॥31॥
2.4.4.32: The day said: Whatever garments and excellent ornaments there were, they gave him, and they fed him with praiseworthy, tasty foods. ॥32॥
2.4.4.33: Brahmā said: Hearing those words of theirs, the destroyer of the cities (Śiva) was satisfied; filled with joy, he lovingly gave abundant gifts to the brāhmaṇas. ॥33॥
2.4.4.34: Receiving news of her son, Pārvatī, delighted at heart, gave to the brāhmaṇas millions of jewels and much wealth. ॥34॥
2.4.4.35: Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, Menā, Sāvitrī, all the women, Viṣṇu, and all the gods gave wealth to the brāhmaṇas. ॥35॥
2.4.4.36: Then that Lord, urged by the gods, sages and mountains, sent messengers—those gaṇas—to where his son was. ॥36॥
2.4.4.37: Vīrabhadra, Viśālākṣa, Śaṅkukarṇa, Karākrama, Nandīśvara, Mahākāla, Vajradaṃṣṭra, Mahonmada, ॥37॥
2.4.4.38: Gokarṇāsya, Dadhimukha, who was like a blazing flame of fire, and a hundred thousand Kṣetrapālas and three hundred thousand bhūtas, ॥38॥
2.4.4.39: and Rudras and Bhairavas, equal to Śiva in prowess, and others of deformed shape, countless, O Nārada. ॥39॥
2.4.4.40: All those messengers of Śiva, bearing various weapons and missiles in their hands, fiercely surrounded the dwelling of the Kṛttikās. ॥40॥
2.4.4.41: Seeing them, all the Kṛttikās, their minds overwhelmed with fear, spoke to Kārttika, who was blazing with brahmic splendour. ॥41॥
2.4.4.42: The Kṛttikās said: Child, countless armies have surrounded our dwelling. What should be done? Where should we go? A great danger has arisen. ॥42॥
2.4.4.43: Kārttikeya said: Give up fear, O auspicious ladies. What fear can there be while I am here? Though a child, I am hard to withstand, O mothers; by whom can I be held back? ॥43॥
2.4.4.44: Brahmā said: Meanwhile, Nandikeśvara, the commander of the army, seated himself there in front of Kārtikeya and spoke. ॥44॥
2.4.4.45: Nandīśvara said: Brother, and you mothers, hear my auspicious news. I have been sent by Maheśa, by Śaṅkara the destroyer. ॥45॥
2.4.4.46: On Kailāsa all the gods, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva and the rest, were assembled in the hall, dear one, at a great festive celebration. ॥46॥
2.4.4.47: Then in the assembly Śivā addressed Śaṅkara, the benefactor of all, and spoke about the matter of searching for you. ॥47॥
2.4.4.48: Śiva questioned those gods one by one about finding you, and they each gave a fitting reply. ॥48॥
2.4.4.49: All of them—Dharma and the others, witnesses of righteous and unrighteous deeds—declared that you, the lord, were here in the abode of the Kṛttikās. ॥49॥
2.4.4.50: Formerly there was secret love-play between Pārvatī and Śiva; and when Śambhu was seen by the gods, his seed fell upon the ground. ॥50॥
2.4.4.51: The Earth cast it into Fire, Fire onto the mountain; that mountain cast it into the Gaṅgā, and by the force of her waves it reached the reed-forest. ॥51॥
2.4.4.52: There you became a child, the lord who accomplishes the gods' task. There you were found by the Kṛttikās. Now go forth to your rightful place. ॥52॥
2.4.4.53: Śambhu together with the gods will perform your consecration. You will obtain all weapons and you will slay the one called Tāraka. ॥53॥
2.4.4.54: You are the son of the destroyer of the universe, and these women are unable to keep you, just as a dry tree cannot hide fire within its own hollow. ॥54॥
2.4.4.55: You are radiant throughout the worlds; you do not shine fittingly in their houses, just as the moon, the king of the twice-born, fallen into a deep well, does not shine. ॥55॥
2.4.4.56: Since you give forth light, you are not hidden from us, because of your brilliance—just as the sun cannot be covered by a man's contrivance. ॥56॥
2.4.4.57: You are Viṣṇu, the pervader of the worlds; you are not born as anything other, O son of Śambhu—just as the all-pervading sky is pervaded by none. ॥57॥
2.4.4.58: You are the lord of yogins, untainted even if you partake in being nourished by them, just as the Self is never tainted by the activities of living beings. ॥58॥
2.4.4.59: You are the origin of the universe and its lord; your dwelling among these women is not fitting. You are a mass of virtues and radiance, as yogins know the Self to be. ॥59॥
2.4.4.60: Brother, men who do not know you are of ruined understanding, just as frogs, though living in the same place, do not value the lotuses. ॥60॥
2.4.4.61: Kārttikeya said: Brother, you know everything, including the knowledge of the three times. You are wise—what praise is enough for you, since you have taken refuge in Mṛtyuñjaya? ॥61॥
2.4.4.62: Whatever wombs beings are born in through their karmas, in those very ones, brother, they find contentment here and now. ॥62॥
2.4.4.63: The Kṛttikās are wise yoginīs, portions of Prakṛti. I have been nourished continually by their milk and kindness. ॥63॥
2.4.4.64: I am their foster-son, and these women are portions of me; they are portions of that Prakṛti, and so I am born of the seed of her lord. ॥64॥
2.4.4.65: My birth was not from the daughter of the lord of mountains, O Nandikeśvara; yet she is my mother by dharma, just as these are—as all agree. ॥65॥
2.4.4.66: You have been sent by Śambhu, and you are great, equal to a son of Śambhu. I shall come with you and see the assembly of gods. ॥66॥
2.4.4.67: Having spoken thus to him, Kārttikeya quickly took leave of the band of Kṛttikās and set out together with Śaṅkara's attendants. ॥67॥
2.4.4.iti: Thus ends the fourth adhyāya, named The search for Kārttikeya and the dialogue with Nandin, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥4॥
2.4.5.1: Brahmā said: Meanwhile, there he saw a superb chariot, wondrous and ever resplendent, built by Viśvakarman. ॥1॥
2.4.5.2: It had a hundred wheels, was very spacious, moved at the speed of thought and was charming; it had been sent by Pārvatī and was surrounded by excellent attendants. ॥2॥
2.4.5.3: Then the infinite Kārttika, supremely wise, born of the seed of the Supreme Lord, mounted it with a grieving heart. ॥3॥
2.4.5.4: At that very moment the Kṛttikās arrived, their hair loosened, stricken with grief, and there, as if maddened, they began to speak these words. ॥4॥
2.4.5.5: The Kṛttikās said: O ocean of compassion, you are going away, abandoning us — you are truly heartless. It is not right that a son who has been reared should forsake his mothers. ॥5॥
2.4.5.6: You were raised by us with love and are rightfully our son. What shall we do? Where shall we go? What indeed are we to do? ॥6॥
2.4.5.7: Having said this, all the Kṛttikās clasped Kārttika to their breasts and quickly fell into a swoon because of separation from their son. ॥7॥
2.4.5.8: Kumāra consoled them with words of spiritual wisdom, and then, O sage, he mounted the chariot together with them and the attendants. ॥8॥
2.4.5.9: Seeing and hearing many auspicious, delightful omens, Kumāra went with the attendants to his father's abode. ॥9॥
2.4.5.10: Accompanied by Nandin, in the swift chariot that moved like the mind, Kumāra reached Kailāsa, at the foot of the imperishable banyan tree. ॥10॥
2.4.5.11: There Kumāra, son of Śaṅkara, skilled in many kinds of play, stayed contentedly with the Kṛttikās and the chief attendants. ॥11॥
2.4.5.12: Then all the hosts of gods, the sages, the Siddhas and Cāraṇas, together with Viṣṇu and Brahmā, announced his arrival. ॥12॥
2.4.5.13: Then, to see Gāṅgeya, Śiva set out joyfully, accompanied by others, by Hari, by Brahmā and by the divine sages. ॥13॥
2.4.5.14: Many conches sounded, kettledrums and trumpets in great numbers; there was a very great festival for the gods, whose hearts were glad. ॥14॥
2.4.5.15: At that very moment all the gaṇas, Vīrabhadra and the rest, followed him closely, making merry, with voices keeping many rhythms. ॥15॥
2.4.5.16: The panegyrists, and those being praised as well, recited his virtues; with joyful minds they shouted victory and salutation. ॥16॥
2.4.5.17: They went to see that unsurpassed son of Śiva, born in the reeds. ॥17॥
2.4.5.18: Pārvatī made auspicious preparations: the charming royal road, adorned with rubies and other gems all around the city. ॥18॥
2.4.5.19: Placing in front the thirty goddesses beginning with Lakṣmī, accompanied by chaste women blessed with husbands and sons, she came forth. ॥19॥
2.4.5.20: At Śiva's command the divine Apsarases, Rambhā and others, smiling and finely attired, devoted themselves to song and dance. ॥20॥
2.4.5.21: Those who beheld Gāṅgeya, the equal of Śaṅkara, saw a great radiance that pervaded the three worlds. ॥21॥
2.4.5.22: All quickly bowed to the boy Kumāra, enveloped in that radiance, gleaming like molten gold, brilliant as the sun. ॥22॥
2.4.5.23: Then they rejoiced, shoulders bent, intent on uttering salutations; coming from left and right, they surrounded him and stood in attendance. ॥23॥
2.4.5.24: I, Viṣṇu, Śakra and likewise all the gods and others fell prostrate on the ground like sticks, surrounding the young Kumāra. ॥24॥
2.4.5.25: Meanwhile Śambhu and the joyful Girijā arrived at the great festival and beheld their son with delight. ॥25॥
2.4.5.26: Then, gazing at his son, the sole friend of the world — the Lord of all, the Supreme Lord himself, adorned with serpent coils and surrounded by the Pramathas — together with the supreme Bhavānī, was filled with the highest joy and affection. ॥26॥
2.4.5.27: Then Skanda, bearer of the spear, seeing Pārvatī and Śiva, swiftly got down from the chariot and bowed with his head. ॥27॥
2.4.5.28: Śiva Śaṅkara, the Supreme Lord, embracing Kumāra with love, gracious and full of affection, lovingly smelled kissed his head. ॥28॥
2.4.5.29: There Pārvatī, overcome with emotion and steeped in affection, embraced Guha and suckled him at her breast, which flowed with milk. ॥29॥
2.4.5.30: Then the joyful gods with their wives performed the ārati-waving for him; the vault of the sky was filled with a great cry of victory. ॥30॥
2.4.5.31: The sages with Vedic chanting, the singers with song, and many others with instruments waited upon young Kumāra there. ॥31॥
2.4.5.32: Then Maheśa, lord of Bhavānī, placing on his lap that young Kumāra blazing with radiance, shone in person, endowed with splendour, the foremost of those blessed with sons. ॥32॥
2.4.5.33: At Śiva's command Kumāra, overjoyed, came to Śiva's abode together with his gaṇas and the greatly enthusiastic gods. ॥33॥
2.4.5.34: Then the divine couple shone there side by side, being worshipped by the sages and surrounded by the best of gods. ॥34॥
2.4.5.35: Kumāra played joyfully on Śiva's lap and squeezed with both hands Vāsuki, who lay on Śiva's neck. ॥35॥
2.4.5.36: Laughing, the compassionate Lord Śambhu, looking with a gracious glance at the child's playful form, then pointed it out to Girijā. ॥36॥
2.4.5.37: Then the blessed Maheśa, together with Girijā, smiling with delight, attained supreme joy; his voice choked with love, the all-pervading sole friend of the world, sole sustainer of the worlds, said nothing at all. ॥37॥
2.4.5.38: Then Śambhu, lord of the world, delighted and following worldly custom, seated Kārttika on a lovely jewelled throne. ॥38॥
2.4.5.39: With joy he bathed him from hundreds of fine jewelled pitchers filled with the waters of all holy places and sanctified by Vedic mantras. ॥39॥
2.4.5.40: Hari gave him a diadem, crown and armlets made of the finest jewels, his own Vaijayantī garland, and a discus. ॥40॥
2.4.5.41: Śiva gave him the trident, the Pināka bow, the battle-axe, the spear, the Pāśupata arrow, the weapon of destruction, and the supreme knowledge. ॥41॥
2.4.5.42: I Brahmā gave the sacred thread, the Vedas and the Mother of the Vedas Gāyatrī, a water-pot, the Brahmā weapon, and the knowledge that crushes enemies. ॥42॥
2.4.5.43: The lord of the gods Indra gave him a lordly elephant and the thunderbolt; the lord of the waters Varuṇa gave a white parasol, a garland of jewels, and the noose. ॥43॥
2.4.5.44: The Sun gave a chariot moving at the speed of mind and armour of great solidity; Yama gave the staff of Yama, and the Moon, store of nectar, a pot of nectar. ॥44॥
2.4.5.45: Fire lovingly gave a great spear to his own son; Nirṛti gave his own weapon, and the Wind the Vāyavya weapon. ॥45॥
2.4.5.46: Kubera gave a mace, Īśa joyfully gave a trident, and all the gods joyfully gave various weapons and devices. ॥46॥
2.4.5.47: Then Kāmadeva, full of joy, gave him the weapon of love; and with supreme joy he gave him a mace and his own lore. ॥47॥
2.4.5.48: The Ocean of Milk gave priceless jewels and a special jewelled anklet; Himālaya gave divine ornaments and garments. ॥48॥
2.4.5.49: Garuḍa gave his own son named Citrabarhaṇa the peacock; Aruṇa gave the strong cock called Tāmracūḍa. ॥49॥
2.4.5.50: Pārvatī, smiling and delighted, with great love gave him supreme, excellent sovereignty and also long life. ॥50॥
2.4.5.51: Lakṣmī joyfully gave divine wealth and a great, charming necklace; Sāvitrī gave the entire knowledge of perfection. ॥51॥
2.4.5.52: And the other goddesses too, O sage, whoever had assembled there, gave gifts to him as to one of their own; so too did the nurses of the child. ॥52॥
2.4.5.53: O best of sages, a very great festival took place there; all attained joy, and especially Śiva and Śivā. ॥53॥
2.4.5.54: At that moment, O sage, the mighty Rudra Bharga, laughing joyfully, spoke to Brahmā and the other gods. ॥54॥
2.4.5.55: Śiva said: O Hari, O Vidhi Brahmā, O gods, all of you listen to my words: I am pleased in every way; choose the boons you desire. ॥55॥
2.4.5.56: Brahmā said: Hearing that speech of Śambhu, O sage, all the gods headed by Viṣṇu, with cheerful faces, spoke to the god Paśupati, the Lord. ॥56॥
2.4.5.57: O Lord, this Tāraka will indeed be slain by Kumāra; it is for that very purpose that this excellent deed has come about. ॥57॥
2.4.5.58: Therefore we shall go this very day, ready to kill Tāraka. Give the command to Kumāra, so that he may kill him for our happiness. ॥58॥
2.4.5.59: Thinking, so be it, the all-pervading Lord, moved by compassion, then gave his son to the gods to kill Tāraka. ॥59॥
2.4.5.60: Then, at Śiva's command, all the gods headed by Brahmā and Viṣṇu, placing Guha in front, together at once went out from the mountain. ॥60॥
2.4.5.61: Having come out from Kailāsa, Tvaṣṭṛ, at Hari's order, built a lovely, wondrous city near the mountain. ॥61॥
2.4.5.62: There Tvaṣṭṛ built for Guha a lovely, divine, wondrous, supremely radiant house, and in it an excellent throne. ॥62॥
2.4.5.63: Then wise Hari, with devotion, had the auspicious consecration of Kārttika performed by the gods with the waters of all sacred places. ॥63॥
2.4.5.64: Having adorned him fully, he installed him there with all his retinue, and lovingly had the rite and festival of Kārttika celebrated. ॥64॥
2.4.5.65: Hari joyfully gave him lordship over the cosmic egg; he marked his forehead with the tilaka and worshipped him together with the gods. ॥65॥
2.4.5.66: Bowing lovingly to Kārttika together with all the gods and sages, he praised with various hymns the eternal one who is the form of Śiva. ॥66॥
2.4.5.67: Seated on the excellent throne, Kārttika shone exceedingly, having attained the state of lordship, protector even of the cosmic egg. ॥67॥
2.4.5.iti: Thus ends the fifth adhyāya, named The consecration of Kumāra, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥5॥
2.4.6.1: Brahmā said: Then and there that son of Gaṅgā (Kārttikeya) displayed a marvel. Listen to it with great delight, O Nārada, for it grants devotion to him. ॥1॥
2.4.6.2: Just then a certain brahmin named Nārada, a glorious performer of sacrifices, came there to seek refuge with Guha. ॥2॥
2.4.6.3: That brahmin, with a gladdened mind, approached Kārttika, bowed deeply, and with auspicious hymns made known his purpose. ॥3॥
2.4.6.4: The brahmin said: Hear my words today, O lord, and ward off my trouble. You are the lord of all the universes; therefore I have come to you for refuge. ॥4॥
2.4.6.5: I had begun to perform a goat-sacrifice (ajamedha). That goat has left my house, having broken its tether. ॥5॥
2.4.6.6: I do not know where it has gone; much searching has been done for it. That strong goat has not been found; hence my sacrifice is being ruined. ॥6॥
2.4.6.7: While you are the protector, O mighty one, how can a sacrifice be ruined? Considering this, O lord of all, fulfil my wish completely. ॥7॥
2.4.6.8: Leaving you, to what refuge should I go, O son of Śiva, O lord — you who are the lord of all universes, well served by all the immortals? ॥8॥
2.4.6.9: You are the friend of the distressed, an ocean of compassion, easy to serve, affectionate to devotees, well praised by Hari, Brahmā and the other gods, the supreme lord; ॥9॥
2.4.6.10: Son of Pārvatī, Skanda, the one supreme, scorcher of foes, the supreme Self, giver of the Self, the lord of the good and of those seeking refuge. ॥10॥
2.4.6.11: O lord of the lowly, great lord, son of Śaṅkara, lord of the three worlds, master, O ruler of māyā, I have come for refuge; protect me, O lover of brahmins. You are lord of all, praised by Brahmā and the other all-knowing gods who bow to you; your form is made of māyā, you give happiness to your devotees, you are intent on protection, the wielder of māyā. ॥11॥
2.4.6.12: You are the life of devotees and a mine of virtues, distinct from the three guṇas, dear to Śambhu; you are Śambhu, Śambhu's son, giving joy when pleased, of the nature of being and consciousness, great; all-knowing, son of Śaṅkara the slayer of Tripura, ever won over by true love; six-faced, fond of the good, fond of those who bow, lord of all, bringer of welfare. O slayer of those who harm the good, O teacher of Śaṅkara, lord of the universe, master, whose feet are served by the immortals and all others — protect me, O you who love service. ॥12॥
2.4.6.13: O terror of enemies, O bringer of welfare, I salute your lotus feet — you who are the refuge of people and the cause of happiness. O Skanda, place my petition in your ear; ever establish devotion to yourself in people's hearts. ॥13॥
2.4.6.14: What can a mighty adversary do to him — even a skilful one guarded on both flanks by his allies? What can even Takṣaka or a flesh-eater do to one whose protector is you, with your able, watchful mind? ॥14॥
2.4.6.15: Even the preceptor of the gods would not be able to praise you; tell me, O most worshipful one, how could I, dull-witted, be able? Pure or impure, ignoble, whatever I may be, O Skanda, I pray for the pollen of your lotus feet. ॥15॥
2.4.6.16: O lord of all, affectionate to devotees, ocean of compassion, I am yours, your own servant; O good master, O lord of the gaṇas, do not count the hundred offences of your servant. O mighty one, remover of your servants' afflictions, you know devotion done anywhere, however little. There is no protector other than you, O Lord, and no man more wretched than I. ॥16॥
2.4.6.17: Maker of welfare, destroyer of the stains of the Kali age, friend of Kubera, with heart moist with compassion, eighteen-eyed, resplendent with six faces — O Guha, make my sacrifice complete. ॥17॥
2.4.6.18: You are the protector of the three worlds, affectionate to those who come for refuge, the performer and the sustainer of sacrifice; you destroy those who create obstacles. ॥18॥
2.4.6.19: O remover of the obstacles of the good, O cause of creation in every way, O lord, O son of Śiva, O embodiment of sacrifice, make my rite complete; salutation to you. ॥19॥
2.4.6.20: You, Skanda, are indeed the protector of all; you alone are the knower of all; you are the lord of all, the ruler, the guardian of every abode. ॥20॥
2.4.6.21: You alone are the knower of music, the knower of the Vedas, the supreme lord; you abide in all, you are the ordainer, the god of gods, the goal of the good. ॥21॥
2.4.6.22: You are the son of Bhavānī, the son of Śambhu, knowledge itself, self-ruling; the meditator and the object of meditation, the father even of the Pitṛs, the source of good souls. ॥22॥
2.4.6.23: Brahmā said: Having heard his words thus, Śiva's son, the sovereign of the gods, sent his attendant (gaṇa) named Vīrabāhu for that purpose. ॥23॥
2.4.6.24: At his command the great hero Vīrabāhu, having bowed to the lord with devotion, went swiftly to search for it. ॥24॥
2.4.6.25: He searched throughout the whole sphere of the universe. He did not find the goat anywhere, but heard of the havoc it was causing. ॥25॥
2.4.6.26: Then he went to Vaikuṇṭha and there saw that goat, very mighty, with the sacrificial post on its neck, causing havoc. ॥26॥
2.4.6.27: The hero seized it by the horns, overpowered it with great force, and brought it before the lord, while it bleated loudly. ॥27॥
2.4.6.28: Seeing it, Lord Kārttika, Guha, who bears the weight of the universe and works great wonders, quickly mounted it. ॥28॥
2.4.6.29: Within a mere muhūrta, O sage, that goat roamed the entire universe, and, merely wearied, quickly came back to that place. ॥29॥
2.4.6.30: Then the lord dismounted and sat on his seat. The goat stood right there, and Nārada spoke to him. ॥30॥
2.4.6.31: Nārada said: Salutation to you, O god, lord of gods; give me the goat, O treasury of compassion. Let me perform the sacrifice joyfully; ah, make me your friend! ॥31॥
2.4.6.32: Kārttikeya said: The goat is not fit to be slain, O brahmin; go to your home, Nārada. Let your entire sacrifice be complete, accomplished by my grace alone. ॥32॥
2.4.6.33: Brahmā said: Having heard thus the lord's words, the brahmin, pleased at heart, gave him an excellent blessing and went to his own home. ॥33॥
2.4.6.iti: Thus ends the sixth adhyāya, named The wonderful deeds of Kumāra, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥6॥
2.4.7.1: Brahmā said: And those gods, Hari and the others, having seen that deed of the Lord, became greatly pleased indeed, their minds settled in faith. ॥1॥
2.4.7.2: Leaping about and roaring, inspired by Śiva's splendour, they placed Kumāra at their head and came to kill Tāraka. ॥2॥
2.4.7.3: Hearing of the gods' preparation, the mighty Tāraka too at once went with a great army to fight against the gods. ॥3॥
2.4.7.4: The gods, seeing Tāraka's great army approaching, though roaring loud lion-roars with all their might, were astonished. ॥4॥
2.4.7.5: Then the celestial voice, the lady of the sky, urged by Śaṅkara, swiftly spoke from above at once to all the gods, Hari and the rest. ॥5॥
2.4.7.6: The heavenly voice said: O gods, you who stand ready with Kumāra placed at your head, having conquered the Daityas in battle, will then be victorious. ॥6॥
2.4.7.7: Brahmā said: Hearing that voice from the sky, all the gods, full of eagerness and shouting heroic cries, then became fearless. ॥7॥
2.4.7.8: With Kumāra at their head, all those gods, their fear gone and eager to fight, went to the place where the land meets the ocean. ॥8॥
2.4.7.9: That Tāraka quickly came to the place where the gods were, together with a great army, surrounded by many Asuras. ॥9॥
2.4.7.10: At his arrival the war-drums sounded, with a din like the clouds of the cosmic dissolution, and other harsh instruments too. ॥10॥
2.4.7.11: Then the Daityas, together with the Asura Tāraka, roared, making the earth tremble with their strides as they leapt about. ॥11॥
2.4.7.12: Hearing that most fierce uproar, all the gods, wholly fearless, rose up as one, eager to fight Tāraka. ॥12॥
2.4.7.13: The lord of the gods, having seated Kumāra on an elephant, went in front, surrounded by a great army of gods and by the guardians of the worlds. ॥13॥
2.4.7.14: Then drums sounded, kettledrums and trumpets in great number, lutes, flutes and mṛdaṅgas, as well as the singing of the Gandharvas. ॥14॥
2.4.7.15: Giving the elephant to great Indra, Kumāra mounted a vehicle made of many marvels and set with various jewels. ॥15॥
2.4.7.16: Having then mounted the aerial car, that greatly renowned son of Śaṅkara, endowed with all virtues and attended by supreme splendour, shone forth magnificently, being fanned with brilliantly gleaming chowries. ॥16॥
2.4.7.17: Then Varuṇa's umbrella, exceedingly radiant, adorned with jewels and resplendent with various gems, was held over Kumāra's head, gleaming with countless moon-like rays of great brilliance. ॥17॥
2.4.7.18: Then all those gods, led by Śakra, assembled, each surrounded by his own forces, mighty and eager for battle. ॥18॥
2.4.7.19: Thus the gods and the Daityas, eager to fight, stood on the earth, each side having arrayed its great army in a separate battle formation. ॥19॥
2.4.7.20: Those two armies of the gods and the Daityas shone facing each other, each eager to slay the other, and being praised by bards. ॥20॥
2.4.7.21: Then both their armies, like forests, roared, terrifying to the utterly unheroic, delightful to the others. ॥21॥
2.4.7.22: Meanwhile there the Daityas and gods, great heroes intoxicated with their strength and overwhelmed with rage, fought one another. ॥22॥
2.4.7.23: There was a most tumultuous battle crowded with gods and Daityas; in a moment everything became strewn with headless trunks and severed heads. ॥23॥
2.4.7.24: There, by hundreds and thousands, warriors esteemed as heroes fell on the ground, slain, their limbs cut off by mighty weapons. ॥24॥
2.4.7.25: In the battle, the arms of some proud heroes were cut off by terrible sword-strokes; the thighs of others were severed. ॥25॥
2.4.7.26: Some had all their limbs crushed by maces and hammers; some, their hearts pierced, were struck down by nooses and javelins. ॥26॥
2.4.7.27: Some were torn open in the back by lances, spears and goads; and severed heads too fell upon the ground. ॥27॥
2.4.7.28: And there many headless trunks were dancing, leaping by hundreds, with weapons raised in their hands. ॥28॥
2.4.7.29: Then hundreds of rivers flowing with blood were set in motion there, and bhūtas, pretas and the like gathered there in hundreds. ॥29॥
2.4.7.30: Jackals and she-jackals were there, devouring much flesh, and likewise vultures, vaṭa-birds, hawks and crows, eaters of flesh, feasted indeed on the abundant flesh of the fallen. ॥30॥
2.4.7.31: Meanwhile there the mighty one named Tāraka at once went with a great army to fight against the gods. ॥31॥
2.4.7.32: Seeing Tāraka, frenzied in battle, approaching eager to fight, the gods, Śakra and the others, then at once advanced; and a great roar arose from both armies. ॥32॥
2.4.7.33: Then indeed began a series of single combats, crushing gods and Asuras, at the sight of which heroes rejoiced and cowards were seized with fear. ॥33॥
2.4.7.34: The mighty son of Diti, Tāraka, fought in battle with Śakra; Saṃhrāda with Agni; and Yama himself with Jambha. ॥34॥
2.4.7.35: Mahāprabhu fought with Nairṛta; the noose-bearer Varuṇa with Bala; Suvīra with Vāyu; and the king of the Guhyakas Kubera with Pavamāna. ॥35॥
2.4.7.36: Śambhu, most skilled in battle, fought with Īśāna; Śumbha fought with Śeṣa, and the Dānava Kumbha with Candra. ॥36॥
2.4.7.37: Kuñjara, of great strength and valour and expert in many kinds of warfare, fought in battle with Mihira using supreme weapons. ॥37॥
2.4.7.38: Thus all the gods and Asuras fought in the conflict in great single combats, resolved on victory through their strength. ॥38॥
2.4.7.39: Vying with one another, those mighty immortals and Daityas proved invincible in that battle of gods and Asuras, O sage. ॥39॥
2.4.7.40: Then there arose a tumultuous battle between those gods and demons, all eager for victory — bringing delight to the heroic and high-spirited, but bringing terror to the others. ॥40॥
2.4.7.41: In that battle the earth then became exceedingly dreadful, impassable and most terrifying, with gods and demons fallen and destroyed in great numbers — yet it brought great joy to the high-spirited. ॥41॥
2.4.7.iti: Thus ends the seventh adhyāya, named The beginning of the battle, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥7॥
2.4.8.1: Brahmā said: Thus, dear son, the extremely tumultuous battle between the armies of the gods and the Dānavas has been described to you. Now hear, O Nārada, the fight of their two lords. ॥1॥
2.4.8.2: Thus, in that extremely tumultuous battle, destructive to gods and Dānavas, the lord of the gods was struck by Tāraka himself with a supreme spear (śakti). ॥2॥
2.4.8.3: At once he fell from his elephant to the ground and became unconscious; the wielder of the thunderbolt, lord of the gods, fell into deep stupor. ॥3॥
2.4.8.4: In the same way, dear son, all the guardians of the worlds were defeated in battle by the far stronger Asuras, skilled in great warfare. ॥4॥
2.4.8.5: Other gods too, fighting with the Daityas, were defeated; unable to bear their might, they were intent only on flight. ॥5॥
2.4.8.6: There the victorious Asuras, their efforts successful, roared, making lion-roars and given to uproar. ॥6॥
2.4.8.7: Meanwhile Vīrabhadra, filled with fury, came there with his heroic Gaṇas and confronted Tāraka, who prided himself on his valour. ॥7॥
2.4.8.8: Putting the gods behind him, the mighty one born of Śiva's wrath, foremost of the Gaṇas, then stood facing him, eager to fight. ॥8॥
2.4.8.9: Then all those Pramathas and the Daityas, in great elation, fought one another in the combat, locked together in the great battle. ॥9॥
2.4.8.10: With tridents, double-edged swords, nooses, swords, axes and spears, those skilled in war struck one another in the fight. ॥10॥
2.4.8.11: Tāraka, struck hard by Vīrabhadra with the trident, suddenly fell to the ground, overwhelmed by a swoon for a moment. ॥11॥
2.4.8.12: Rising quickly, the hero Tāraka, best of the Daityas, regaining consciousness, forcefully struck Vīrabhadra with his spear. ॥12॥
2.4.8.13: Likewise the hero Vīrabhadra, of great splendour, swiftly struck Tāraka with his terrible, sharp trident. ॥13॥
2.4.8.14: Then Tāraka too, lord of the sons of Diti, very powerful and esteemed by heroes, struck Vīrabhadra in the fight with his spear. ॥14॥
2.4.8.15: Thus fighting, the two, skilled in the science of war, struck each other in the combat with many kinds of missiles and weapons. ॥15॥
2.4.8.16: Then a single combat took place there between those two great beings, tumultuous and hair-raising, while all looked on. ॥16॥
2.4.8.17: Then kettledrums, mṛdaṅgas, paṭahas, ānakas and gomukhas, beaten by the warriors, resounded, most terrifying to those who heard. ॥17॥
2.4.8.18: Fully armoured, battered by blows, the two fought each other in great fury, like Budha and Aṅgāraka (Mercury and Mars). ॥18॥
2.4.8.19: Seeing then such a fight of Vīrabhadra with him, you, dear to Śiva, went there and spoke to Vīrabhadra. ॥19॥
2.4.8.20: Nārada said: O Vīrabhadra, great hero, you are the leader of the Gaṇas. Turn back from this battle; his slaying by you is not desired. ॥20॥
2.4.8.21: Hearing these words of yours, Vīrabhadra, leader of the Gaṇas, though filled with anger, then spoke to you with joined palms. ॥21॥
2.4.8.22: Vīrabhadra said: O best of sages, most wise one, hear my supreme words: I will slay Tāraka. Behold my valour today. ॥22॥
2.4.8.23: Those warriors who bring their master into the arena of battle are sinners and great cowards; having gone to battle, they perish. ॥23॥
2.4.8.24: They attain an evil destiny, and hell is certain for them. Know me to be Vīrabhadra; I should never be addressed thus by you. ॥24॥
2.4.8.25: Those who fight fearlessly, their limbs pierced by weapons and missiles, are praiseworthy here and hereafter and obtain wondrous happiness. ॥25॥
2.4.8.26: Let the gods headed by Hari hear my words: today, without the help of my master, I will make the earth free of Tāraka. ॥26॥
2.4.8.27: Having said this, Vīrabhadra, bearing the trident, together with the Pramathas, meditated on Śambhu in his mind and fought with Tāraka. ॥27॥
2.4.8.28: Joined in battle with many great heroes mounted on bulls, three-eyed and bearing excellent tridents, he shone forth. ॥28॥
2.4.8.29: Raising an uproar, the fearless Gaṇas in hundreds, placing Vīrabhadra at their head, fought with the Dānavas. ॥29॥
2.4.8.30: Those Asuras too, who lived by Tāraka, fierce in strength and great heroes, fought, crushing the Gaṇas in fury. ॥30॥
2.4.8.31: Again and again there was a fierce clash of the Gaṇas with the foremost Daityas. Then those Gaṇas, rejoicing and expert in supreme weapons, became victorious. ॥31॥
2.4.8.32: Defeated by the mighty Gaṇas, those Asuras turned away from battle and took to flight, distressed and agitated in mind. ॥32॥
2.4.8.33: Seeing his army thus routed, its protector, the Asura Tāraka, filled with rage, went forth to slay the hosts of the gods. ॥33॥
2.4.8.34: Assuming ten thousand arms and mounting a lion swiftly, he felled those gods and Gaṇas at the forefront of battle. ॥34॥
2.4.8.35: Seeing that deed of his, Vīrabhadra, the very mighty leader of the Gaṇas, became greatly enraged, resolved on his slaying. ॥35॥
2.4.8.36: Remembering the lotus feet of Śiva, he seized his supreme trident; by its splendour all the quarters and the sky blazed. ॥36॥
2.4.8.37: Meanwhile the Lord (Kumāra), a witness of great wonders, at once restrained him and those headed by Vīrabāhu from the battle. ॥37॥
2.4.8.38: By his command Vīrabhadra then withdrew from the battle. Thereupon the great hero Tāraka, leader of the Asuras, became enraged. ॥38॥
2.4.8.39: Then the Asura released a shower of arrows upon the gods; inflamed with wrath, skilled in battle with many weapons, he at once challenged the gods. ॥39॥
2.4.8.40: Having thus done a mighty deed, Tāraka, protector of the Asuras, best of the strong, was invincible to all the gods. ॥40॥
2.4.8.41: Seeing those gods, overwhelmed with fear, being struck down in this way, Acyuta grew angry and quickly made himself ready for battle. ॥41॥
2.4.8.42: Taking up the discus Sudarśana and the bow Śārṅga, the armed Lord Hari advanced against the great demon for battle. ॥42॥
2.4.8.43: Then there arose a great battle between Hari and Tāraka, hair-raising and exceedingly fierce, while all looked on, O sage. ॥43॥
2.4.8.44: Raising his mace, Hari struck the demon with force; the mighty demon split it in two with his trident. ॥44॥
2.4.8.45: Then the Lord, who grants fearlessness to the gods, enraged, struck the leader of the demons with volleys of arrows released from Śārṅga. ॥45॥
2.4.8.46: That demon Tāraka too, a great hero and slayer of enemy heroes, swiftly cut down all the arrows with his own sharp shafts. ॥46॥
2.4.8.47: Then the demon Tāraka quickly struck Murāri with his spear; stunned by that blow, Hari fell to the ground. ॥47॥
2.4.8.48: Rising up in a moment, Acyuta in fury seized his discus, ablaze with flaming fire, letting out a great lion's roar. ॥48॥
2.4.8.49: With it Hari struck that lord of the demons; pained by that mighty blow, he fell to the ground. ॥49॥
2.4.8.50: Rising again, Tāraka, king of the Daityas and leader of the demons, endowed with great strength, swiftly shattered the discus with his spear. ॥50॥
2.4.8.51: Again with that great spear he struck the beloved of the immortals; Acyuta too, the great hero, struck him with his sword Nandaka. ॥51॥
2.4.8.52: Thus the demon and Viṣṇu, both mighty, fought each other at length there in battle, their strength undiminished, O sage. ॥52॥
2.4.8.iti: Thus ends the eighth adhyāya, named The general battle of the gods and the Daityas, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥8॥
2.4.9.1: Brahmā said: O God of gods, Guha, lord, son of Śaṅkara, son of Pārvatī, this battle between Viṣṇu and the demon Tāraka is pointless and does not befit them. ॥1॥
2.4.9.2: That exceedingly mighty Tāraka cannot be slain by Viṣṇu, for he has received a boon from me. I tell you the truth, the truth. ॥2॥
2.4.9.3: O son of Pārvatī, there is no other slayer of this sinner except you. Therefore, O great lord, you must carry out my word. ॥3॥
2.4.9.4: O scorcher of foes, quickly make yourself ready to slay the demon. It was for his slaying that you were born from Śaṅkara, O son of Śivā. ॥4॥
2.4.9.5: Protect, protect, O great hero, the gods who are distressed in battle. You are not a child, nor even a youth, but the lord, the master of all. ॥5॥
2.4.9.6: See Śakra, and Viṣṇu too, in distress, and the gods and the gaṇas. Slay this great demon and make the three worlds happy. ॥6॥
2.4.9.7: Formerly Indra, together with the guardians of the worlds, was conquered by him, and even the great hero Viṣṇu was humiliated through the power of his austerity. ॥7॥
2.4.9.8: The entire three worlds were conquered by this wicked demon. Now, because of your presence, they the gods have waged battle once again. ॥8॥
2.4.9.9: Therefore Tāraka, that sinful being, must be slain by you. By virtue of my boon he cannot be killed by anyone else, O son of Śaṅkara. ॥9॥
2.4.9.10: Hearing these words of mine, Kumāra, the son of Śaṅkara, laughed with a pleased heart and said, so be it. ॥10॥
2.4.9.11: Having resolved upon slaying the demon, that great lord, the son of Śaṅkara, then descended from his aerial chariot and went on foot. ॥11॥
2.4.9.12: Then, running about on foot, that supremely heroic Kumāra, born of Śiva, shone brilliantly, holding in his hand that spear of great radiance, blazing with splendour like a great meteor. ॥12॥
2.4.9.13: Seeing him approach—exceedingly fierce, unperturbed, six-faced, immeasurable—the demon said to the foremost of the gods: Is this Kumāra the slayer of his enemies? ॥13॥
2.4.9.14: I, the peerless hero, shall fight with him, and I alone shall fight all the heroes. I shall slay all the gaṇas too, together with the world-guardians and those led by Hari. ॥14॥
2.4.9.15: Having spoken thus, that mighty one then set out to fight, aiming at Kumāra. Seizing a most wondrous spear, Tāraka addressed the foremost gods. ॥15॥
2.4.9.16: Tāraka said: How is it that you have put Kumāra before me today? You gods are shameless—especially Śakra and Keśava. ॥16॥
2.4.9.17: Formerly these two did deeds opposed to the path of the Veda. Listen to what I declare; I shall describe it in detail. ॥17॥
2.4.9.18: Of these, Viṣṇu is a deceiver, a wrongdoer, and especially lacking in discernment—he by whom Bali was formerly bound, sinfully resorting to trickery. ॥18॥
2.4.9.19: It was by him too that long ago the two demons Madhu and Kaiṭabha were deliberately beheaded through cunning, and the Vedic path was abandoned. ॥19॥
2.4.9.20: In the form of Mohinī he made a distinction between the rows of diners at the drinking of nectar by gods and demons, and so the Vedic path was violated. ॥20॥
2.4.9.21: Becoming Rāma, he killed a woman, and he struck down Vālī. Then he slew Vaiśravaṇa Rāvaṇa, a brāhmaṇa, and the ordinance of scripture was destroyed. ॥21॥
2.4.9.22: That his own wife, though sinless, was abandoned by him who delights in sin—there too the Vedic path was destroyed for the sake of his own interest. ॥22॥
2.4.9.23: In the incarnation so named (rasākhyaka) as Paraśurāma he cut off his own mother's head, and this wicked one also insulted the son of his preceptor. ॥23॥
2.4.9.24: Becoming Kṛṣṇa, he defiled other men's women against the law of family, and likewise contracted his own marriages abandoning the Vedic way. ॥24॥
2.4.9.25: And again, in his ninth birth, the Vedic path was reviled, and a heretical doctrine opposed to the Vedic path was established. ॥25॥
2.4.9.26: How can he who has committed such sin, forsaking the Vedic path, win in battle or be the foremost of the righteous? ॥26॥
2.4.9.27: And Śakra, who is his elder brother, is held to be a great sinner; many sins were committed by him for his own ends. ॥27॥
2.4.9.28: Diti's embryo was cut up by him, especially for his own interest; Gautama's wife was violated; and Vṛtra, born of a brāhmaṇa, was slain. ॥28॥
2.4.9.29: And the heads of the brāhmaṇa Viśvarūpa, a sister's son and a preceptor, were cut off—thereby the path of the Veda was destroyed. ॥29॥
2.4.9.30: Having committed many sins again and again, Hari and Śakra have had their splendour struck down and are especially bereft of valour. ॥30॥
2.4.9.31: Through their strength you will not gain victory in battle. Why, having fallen into folly, have you come here to lose your lives? ॥31॥
2.4.9.32: These two, their minds greedy for self-interest, do not know dharma. O immortals, without dharma every undertaking becomes fruitless. ॥32॥
2.4.9.33: These two most impudent ones have today placed a child in front of me. I shall kill the boy, and that sin too will be theirs. ॥33॥
2.4.9.34: But let the boy go far away from here if he wishes to save his life. Having said this, aiming at the two Haris, Viṣṇu and Indra, he spoke to Vīrabhadra. ॥34॥
2.4.9.35: Formerly at Dakṣa's sacrifice you killed many brāhmaṇas. Today, O sinless one, I shall show you the fruit of that deed. ॥35॥
2.4.9.36: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, and having shaken off his own merit through that act of reviling them, Tāraka, the foremost of warriors, seized a most wondrous spear. ॥36॥
2.4.9.37: As the demon Tāraka came forcefully near the boy, Śakra, with Guha at his front, struck him with the thunderbolt. ॥37॥
2.4.9.38: Shattered by that blow of the thunderbolt, Tāraka, his strength sapped by his reviling, suddenly fell to the ground for a moment. ॥38॥
2.4.9.39: Though fallen, he rose up and in rage struck him with his spear, and threw Purandara, mounted on his elephant, down to the ground. ॥39॥
2.4.9.40: When Purandara fell, a great cry of lament arose, and seeing that, distress entered the army of the gods. ॥40॥
2.4.9.41: Hear from me what painful deed Tāraka also did right there, a deed contrary to dharma that became the cause of his own destruction. ॥41॥
2.4.9.42: Trampling with his foot on Indra, who had fallen, and seizing the thunderbolt from his hand, he struck Śakra hard again with a blow of the raised thunderbolt. ॥42॥
2.4.9.43: Seeing Śakra thus humiliated, the mighty Lord Viṣṇu raised his discus and struck Tāraka. ॥43॥
2.4.9.44: Struck by the blow of the discus, he fell to the ground; but rising again, the lord of the Daityas struck that Viṣṇu with his spear. ॥44॥
2.4.9.45: By that blow of the spear Acyuta fell to the earth; there was a great cry of alas, and the gods wailed greatly. ॥45॥
2.4.9.46: In the twinkling of an eye, even as Viṣṇu was rising again by himself, Vīrabhadra arrived at that very moment and faced the Asura. ॥46॥
2.4.9.47: Raising his trident, the mighty and powerful Vīrabhadra violently struck Tāraka, the overlord of the sons of Diti. ॥47॥
2.4.9.48: By that blow of the trident he then fell to the ground; yet though fallen, the greatly radiant Tāraka rose again. ॥48॥
2.4.9.49: Growing furious, the great hero, leader of all the Asuras, then struck Vīrabhadra on the chest with his supreme spear. ॥49॥
2.4.9.50: Vīrabhadra too, struck hard on the chest by that supreme spear hurled in anger, fell to the ground, unconscious for a moment. ॥50॥
2.4.9.51: The gods with the Gaṇas, and the Gandharvas, serpents and Rākṣasas, cried out again and again with a great wail of alas. ॥51॥
2.4.9.52: Within a mere instant, suddenly, that greatly vigourous Vīrabhadra, slayer of enemies, raising his trident gleaming like lightning, shone forth blazing with radiance. ॥52॥
2.4.9.53: That trident illumined the expanse of the directions with its own lustre; its disc was like the orbs of the sun, the moon and fire; it was of great brilliance, terrifying to heroes, supreme, called Kāla, utterly destructive, and intensely blazing. ॥53॥
2.4.9.54: Just as the mighty Vīrabhadra was then about to slay the Asura with the trident, he was restrained by Kumāra. ॥54॥
2.4.9.iti: Thus ends the ninth adhyāya, named The words of Tāraka and the battle of Śakra, Viṣṇu and Vīrabhadra, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥9॥
2.4.10.1: Brahmā said: Having restrained that Vīrabhadra, Kumāra, the slayer of enemy heroes, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva, resolved upon the killing of Tāraka. ॥1॥
2.4.10.2: Then the greatly radiant, mighty Kārttikeya roared; armed for battle and enraged, he stood surrounded by a great army. ॥2॥
2.4.10.3: Then all the hosts of gods cried victory, victory, and at that very moment he was praised with pleasing words by the divine sages. ॥3॥
2.4.10.4: Then arose a battle between Tāraka and Kumāra, exceedingly hard to endure, most dreadful, terrifying to all beings. ॥4॥
2.4.10.5: Those two heroes, spears in hand, fought each other there, O sage, while all looked on in great amazement. ॥5॥
2.4.10.6: Their bodies pierced by spears, the two, equipped with great means of war, kept deceiving each other like two mighty lions. ॥6॥
2.4.10.7: Adopting the Vaitālika mode, likewise the Khecaraka method, and adopting the Prāpata, they struck spear against spear. ॥7॥
2.4.10.8: With these techniques the two great heroes, of great strength and valour, each becoming a practitioner against the other, waged a wondrous battle. ॥8॥
2.4.10.9: Exerting great force, each seeking the other's death, the two experts in warfare struck in battle with torrents of spear-blows. ॥9॥
2.4.10.10: On the head, the neck, the thighs, the knees, the hips, the breast, the chest and the back, they cut into each other. ॥10॥
2.4.10.11: Then those two mighty ones, fighting and eager to kill, leaping about with heroic shouts, skilled in many kinds of combat— ॥11॥
2.4.10.12: All the gods, Gandharvas and Kinnaras became spectators; they said to one another there: Who will win in this battle? ॥12॥
2.4.10.13: Then a voice from the sky spoke, consoling the gods: This Kumāra will kill the demon Tāraka here. ॥13॥
2.4.10.14: Let all the gods not grieve; let them remain at ease. For Śaṅkara himself has taken his stand in the form of a son for your sake. ॥14॥
2.4.10.15: Hearing then that auspicious voice uttered in the sky, young Kumāra, surrounded by the Pramathas, became gladdened and quickly eager to slay Tāraka, lord of the Daityas. ॥15॥
2.4.10.16: Filled with wrath, the mighty-armed Kumāra forcefully struck the demon Tāraka between the breasts with that spear. ॥16॥
2.4.10.17: Disregarding that blow, Tāraka, chief of the Daityas, greatly enraged, in turn struck Kumāra with his own spear. ॥17॥
2.4.10.18: By that spear-blow Śiva's son fell unconscious; after a moment he regained consciousness, being praised by the great sages. ॥18॥
2.4.10.19: Like a lion maddened with rage, eager to kill, so the valiant Kumāra struck the demon Tāraka with his spear. ॥19॥
2.4.10.20: Thus the two, Kumāra and Tāraka, both skilled in spear-fighting, fought each other in extreme fury. ॥20॥
2.4.10.21: Each wishing to defeat the other, they were wholly intent on their practised skill, fighting on foot, wondrous in appearance and swift. ॥21॥
2.4.10.22: With volleys of various blows they struck each other, executing many manoeuvres, roaring, of excellent valour. ॥22॥
2.4.10.23: All the gods, Gandharvas and Kinnaras, intent on watching, were struck with supreme amazement; they said nothing there. ॥23॥
2.4.10.24: The wind did not blow, the sun became lustreless, and the whole earth with its mountains, woods and forests shook. ॥24॥
2.4.10.25: Meanwhile the mountains headed by Himālaya, distressed out of affection, came there, wishing to protect Kumāra. ॥25॥
2.4.10.26: Then Śiva's son, the son of Girijā, seeing all those mountains stricken with fear, spoke to them, reassuring them. ॥26॥
2.4.10.27: Kumāra said: Do not be troubled, O blessed ones; do not worry, O mountains. Today I shall slay this most wicked one while all of you look on. ॥27॥
2.4.10.28: Having thus comforted the mountains and the hosts of immortals, and having bowed to Girijā and Śambhu, he took up his brilliantly shining spear. ॥28॥
2.4.10.29: Resolved to kill that Tāraka, spear in hand, the great lord, the mighty hero Kumāra, child of Śambhu, shone forth. ॥29॥
2.4.10.30: Then Kumāra, rich with the radiance of Śaṅkara, struck with that spear the demon Tāraka, the tormentor of the worlds. ॥30॥
2.4.10.31: Instantly and suddenly the demon named Tāraka, the great hero, lord of all the hosts of Asuras, fell to the ground, his limbs shattered. ॥31॥
2.4.10.32: Slain by Kumāra, that exceedingly heroic Tāraka indeed perished right there, O sage, as all looked on. ॥32॥
