2.4.10.33: Seeing the very powerful Tāraka thus fallen, the hero did not strike him again, since he had become lifeless in the battle. ॥33॥
2.4.10.34: When that mighty great Daitya named Tāraka was slain, many Asuras were then brought to destruction by the hosts of gods. ॥34॥
2.4.10.35: Some, frightened, stood with joined palms there in the battle; some Daityas, their limbs cut and pierced, died by thousands. ॥35॥
2.4.10.36: Some Daityas, seeking refuge, then took refuge with Kumāra, saying with joined palms, protect us, protect us. ॥36॥
2.4.10.37: Many were killed there and many fled; as they fled, distressed, they were beaten by the hosts of the immortals. ॥37॥
2.4.10.38: By thousands they entered Pātāla, wishing to save their lives; all of them fleeing, their hopes broken, sank into misery. ॥38॥
2.4.10.39: Thus the entire Daitya army was routed, O lord of sages; none remained there then, out of fear of the Gaṇas and the gods. ॥39॥
2.4.10.40: When that wicked one was slain, everything became free of thorns; then all those gods, Śakra and the rest, attained happiness. ॥40॥
2.4.10.41: When Kumāra had thus won victory, all the gods were delighted at once, and the three worlds were filled with great happiness. ॥41॥
2.4.10.42: Then Śiva too, learning of Kārttika's victory, came there joyfully with his attendants (gaṇas) and his beloved. ॥42॥
2.4.10.43: Placing his own son Kumāra, radiant as the sun, on his lap, he fondled him with great love; and Śivā, overflowing with affection, did so too. ॥43॥
2.4.10.44: Then Himālaya came, surrounded by his sons, with his kinsmen and followers, and praised Śambhu, Śivā and Guha. ॥44॥
2.4.10.45: Then all the hosts of gods, the sages, the Siddhas and Cāraṇas praised Śaṅkara's son, Śambhu, and Girijā, who was greatly pleased. ॥45॥
2.4.10.46: Then the demigods showered a very great rain of flowers; the lords of the Gandharvas sang and the troupes of Apsarases danced. ॥46॥
2.4.10.47: Likewise musical instruments sounded at that time especially, and cries of victory and obeisance rose loudly again and again. ॥47॥
2.4.10.48: Then I Brahmā and Acyuta too became especially delighted, and with great reverence praised Śiva, Śivā and Kumāra. ॥48॥
2.4.10.49: Placing Kumāra in front, the gods headed by Hari and Indra, and likewise other sages, lovingly performed the nīrājana (waving of lights). ॥49॥
2.4.10.50: With the sound of songs and instruments and abundant Vedic chanting, there was then a great festival, and especially much glorification. ॥50॥
2.4.10.51: O sage, the Lord of the world was praised by all the hosts of gods, delighted, with songs and instruments and with joined palms. ॥51॥
2.4.10.52: Then the blessed Rudra, praised by all, went with Bhavānī, the Mother of the world, to his own mountain, surrounded by his gaṇas. ॥52॥
2.4.10.iti: Thus ends the tenth adhyāya, named The slaying of the demon Tāraka and the festival of the gods, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥10॥
2.4.11.1: Brahmā said: Meanwhile, O sage, the mountain named Krauñca, tormented by Bāṇa, came there to Kumāra for refuge. ॥1॥
2.4.11.2: He Bāṇa, who had fled from the battle unable to bear the lordly splendour of Kumāra, and who was endowed with the strength of ten thousand crores, harassed Krauñca exceedingly. ॥2॥
2.4.11.3: Bowing with devotion at Kumāra's lotus feet, he reverently praised Guha with words full of love. ॥3॥
2.4.11.4: Krauñca said: O Kumāra, O Skanda, lord of the gods, destroyer of the demon Tāraka, protect me, who have come for refuge, sorely oppressed by the demon Bāṇa. ॥4॥
2.4.11.5: O Mahāsena, routed in battle with you, he fled, and coming to me he oppressed me. Alas, O lord, mine of compassion! ॥5॥
2.4.11.6: Tormented by him, I have come fleeing to your refuge in great distress. O lord of the gods, O reed-born one, show mercy. ॥6॥
2.4.11.7: O mighty one, destroy that demon called Bāṇa and make me happy. You especially are the slayer of demons, the protector of the gods, the self-ruling sovereign. ॥7॥
2.4.11.8: Brahmā said: Thus praised by Krauñca, Skanda, protector of devotees, was pleased; taking up his own incomparable spear, the auspicious one meditated on Śiva in his mind. ॥8॥
2.4.11.9: The son of Śaṅkara hurled it, aiming at Bāṇa. Then there arose a great sound, and the directions and the sky blazed. ॥9॥
2.4.11.10: Having reduced that demon together with his army to ashes in a mere instant, that supreme spear returned to Guha's side, O sage. ॥10॥
2.4.11.11: Then Lord Kumāra said to Krauñca, the best of mountains: Go to your home without fear; that demon has perished with his army. ॥11॥
2.4.11.12: Hearing those words of the lord, the king of mountains was then delighted; having praised Guha, the foe of that demon, he returned to his own abode. ॥12॥
2.4.11.13: Then, O sage, Skanda joyfully installed there, according to rite, three liṅgas of Maheśa that destroy sin. ॥13॥
2.4.11.14: First the one named Pratijñeśvara, then reverently Kapāleśvara, and then Kumāreśvara — the triad that grants every attainment. ॥14॥
2.4.11.15: Further, Guha, lord of all, joyfully installed there, near the pillar of victory, a liṅga named Stambheśvara. ॥15॥
2.4.11.16: Then all the gods there, Viṣṇu and the others, joyfully installed liṅgas of the trident-bearing god of gods. ॥16॥
2.4.11.17: Then the glory of all those Śiva-liṅgas became wondrous; it grants all desires and also bestows liberation on those who practise devotion. ॥17॥
2.4.11.18: Then all the gods headed by Viṣṇu, glad at heart, wished to go to the best of mountains Kailāsa, joyfully placing Guha at their head. ॥18॥
2.4.11.19: At that moment Śeṣa's son, named Kumuda, oppressed by a demon, came to Kumāra for refuge. ॥19॥
2.4.11.20: The demon called Pralamba, who had fled from this battle — that mighty follower of Tāraka was causing havoc there. ॥20॥
2.4.11.21: Then Kumuda, the great son of Śeṣa, lord of serpents, having come to Kumāra for refuge, praised the son of Girijā. ॥21॥
2.4.11.22: Kumuda said: O god of gods, great god, excellent dear one, great lord, I am tormented by Pralamba; I have come to you for refuge. ॥22॥
2.4.11.23: Protect me, who have sought refuge, oppressed by the demon Pralamba, O Kumāra, Skanda, lord of gods, foe of Tāraka, great lord. ॥23॥
2.4.11.24: You are the friend of the afflicted, an ocean of compassion, loving to those who bow down; you are indeed the punisher of the wicked, the giver of refuge and the goal of the good. ॥24॥
2.4.11.25: Thus praised by Kumuda and entreated for his Pralamba's slaying, he took up his own spear, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva. ॥25॥
2.4.11.26: The son of Girijā hurled it, aiming at Pralamba. Then there arose a great sound, and the directions and the sky blazed. ॥26॥
2.4.11.27: The spear, which acts without effort, swiftly reduced him with his ten thousand forces to ashes and suddenly returned to Guha's side. ॥27॥
2.4.11.28: Then Kumāra said to Kumuda, the serpent youth: Go to your home without fear; that demon has perished with his army. ॥28॥
2.4.11.29: Hearing Guha's words, Kumuda, son of the lord of serpents, praised Kumāra, bowed to him, and joyfully went to Pātāla. ॥29॥
2.4.11.30: Thus, O lord of sages, I have described to you Kumāra's victory, the deed of Tāraka's slaying, which causes supreme wonder. ॥30॥
2.4.11.31: It is divine, removes all sins, grants all desires to men; it is auspicious, bestows fame and long life, and gives enjoyment and liberation to the good. ॥31॥
2.4.11.32: Those men, endowed with boundless good fortune, who recite the glorious, divine story of Kumāra, go to Śiva's world. ॥32॥
2.4.11.33: And those people who, full of faith, listen with devotion to his glory will enjoy supreme happiness here and attain divine liberation. ॥33॥
2.4.11.iti: Thus ends the eleventh adhyāya, named The slaying of Bāṇa and Pralamba and the victory of Kumāra, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥11॥
2.4.12.1: Brahmā said: Seeing Tāraka slain, the gods headed by Viṣṇu, and all the others with joyful faces, praised Śaṅkara's son with devotion. ॥1॥
2.4.12.2: The gods said: Obeisance to you whose form is auspicious; obeisance to you, O auspiciousness of the universe. O friend of the universe, obeisance be to you; obeisance to you, O maker of the universe. ॥2॥
2.4.12.3: Obeisance be to you, slayer of the foremost of the Dānavas, taker of Bāṇāsura's life, O god; to the destroyer of Pralamba, whose form is pure, again and again obeisance to you, O child of Śaṅkara. ॥3॥
2.4.12.4: You alone are the creator and sustainer of the worlds; you alone are the destroyer, O son of Śuci (Agni) — be gracious. The image of the world is your manifest form; be gracious, O son of Śambhu, friend of the distressed. ॥4॥
2.4.12.5: O protector of the gods, O master, protect us always, O lord; O preserver of the gods' lives, be gracious, O mine of compassion. ॥5॥
2.4.12.6: By slaying the demon Tāraka together with his retinue, O all-pervading one, you have freed all the gods from calamities, O supreme lord. ॥6॥
2.4.12.7: Brahmā said: Thus praised by the gods headed by Viṣṇu, that lord Kumāra gave new boons to all of them in turn, O sage. ॥7॥
2.4.12.8: Then that son of Giriśa, seeing the mountains praising him, became exceedingly pleased and spoke, granting boons. ॥8॥
2.4.12.9: Skanda said: All of you mountains shall indeed be worthy of worship by ascetics, and shall be resorted to by men of ritual action and men of knowledge. ॥9॥
2.4.12.10: By my word, O mountains, you shall become distinguished forms of Śambhu and forms of the liṅga as well — there is no doubt. ॥10॥
2.4.12.11: This Himavat, best of mountains, who is now my maternal grandfather, most fortunate, shall indeed be the giver of fruits to ascetics. ॥11॥
2.4.12.12: The gods said: Having thus given boons and slain Tāraka, lord of the asuras, you have made all of us, moving and unmoving, happy. ॥12॥
2.4.12.13: Now indeed, with great love, you should go to Kailāsa, the abode of Giriśa, to see your mother and father, Śivā and Śambhu. ॥13॥
2.4.12.14: Brahmā said: Having said this, all the gods headed by Viṣṇu, having received his consent, held a great festival on a grand scale and went with Kumāra to the mountain. ॥14॥
2.4.12.15: As the lord Kumāra went to Kailāsa, the abode of Śaṅkara, a great auspicious tumult arose and there was the cry of victory. ॥15॥
2.4.12.16: That Kumāra mounted an aerial car of supreme splendour, adorned on every side, delightful, shining above all. ॥16॥
2.4.12.17: Then I and Viṣṇu, both joyful, held chowries over Guha's head with great love, O sage, and were tireless. ॥17॥
2.4.12.18: Indra and all the other immortals, rendering service to Guha as was fitting, went along then in the four directions, delighted. ॥18॥
2.4.12.19: Proclaiming Śambhu's victory, they reached Śambhu's mountain; joyfully they entered, and there an auspicious sound was raised. ॥19॥
2.4.12.20: Seeing Śiva and Śivā, all of them, Viṣṇu and the others, quickly bowed with devotion to Śaṅkara, joining their palms, humbly. ॥20॥
2.4.12.21: Kumāra too, humble in spirit, descended from the aerial car and joyfully bowed to Śambhu and to Śivā seated on the lion-throne. ॥21॥
2.4.12.22: Then, seeing that Kumāra, their son dear as life, the divine couple Śiva and Śivā rejoiced exceedingly, O Nārada. ॥22॥
2.4.12.23: The great lord lifted him up and seated him on his lap; out of affection he joyfully smelled his head and caressed him with his hand. ॥23॥
2.4.12.24: Filled with great bliss, Śambhu, out of great affection, kissed the face of Kumāra, the great lord, the enemy of Tāraka. ॥24॥
2.4.12.25: Śivā too lifted him up and seated him on her own lap; out of great affection, placing her hand on his head, she kissed his lotus-face. ॥25॥
2.4.12.26: Then the great joy of the two, the couple Śiva and Śivā, who were acting in worldly fashion, grew exceedingly, O Nārada, dear one. ॥26॥
2.4.12.27: Then there was a great festival, full of many wonders, in Śiva's abode; cries of victory and of obeisance rang out exceedingly on all sides. ॥27॥
2.4.12.28: Then all the hosts of gods headed by Viṣṇu, and likewise the sages, bowing reverently with joy to Śambhu, praised him together with Śivā, O sage. ॥28॥
2.4.12.29: The gods said: O god of gods, O Mahādeva, giver of fearlessness to devotees, obeisance, obeisance to you many times over, O mine of compassion, O Maheśvara. ॥29॥
2.4.12.30: Wondrous is your great divine play, O Mahādeva, bestowing happiness on all the virtuous, O Śaṅkara, friend of the distressed, great lord. ॥30॥
2.4.12.31: Being thus dull-minded and ignorant, we do not know the eternal mode of invocation in your worship, nor indeed your wondrous ways, O lord. ॥31॥
2.4.12.32: To the bearer of the stream of Gaṅgā's waters, to the support of all, to the one whose nature is the guṇas, obeisance to you, lord of the thirty gods; to Śaṅkara obeisance again and again. ॥32॥
2.4.12.33: Obeisance to the one bearing the bull emblem, to the great lord, to the lord of the gaṇas; obeisance to the lord of all, the god, the lord of the three worlds. ॥33॥
2.4.12.34: To the destroyer of all the worlds, O lord, obeisance, obeisance to you; to the sustainer and creator, O lord of gods, to the lord of the three guṇas, the eternal one. ॥34॥
2.4.12.35: To the unattached one, the supreme lord, to Śiva, the supreme Self, to the one beyond the manifest world, the pure, the supreme and the imperishable. ॥35॥
2.4.12.36: Obeisance to you, staff in hand, who are Kāla (Time), noose in hand; obeisance to you, foremost of the Vedic mantras, the hundred-tongued. ॥36॥
2.4.12.37: Whatever was, is, and will be, whatever is stationary and moving — all has arisen entirely from your body, O supreme lord. ॥37॥
2.4.12.38: Protect us always, O master; be gracious, O blessed lord. We have taken refuge in you completely, O supreme lord. ॥38॥
2.4.12.39: Obeisance to you, the dark-throated Rudra, who are the svāhā-utterance; obeisance to you, formless, with form, and of universal form. ॥39॥
2.4.12.40: To Śiva, the blue-throated, who bears pyre-ash on his limbs, to the one ever blue-crested, to Śrīkaṇṭha, obeisance again and again. ॥40॥
2.4.12.41: To him before whom all bodies bow, to him who is bowed to through self-restraint, to Mahādeva, to Śarva, and to him whose feet are worshipped by all — salutations. ॥41॥
2.4.12.42: Among all the gods you are Brahmā; among the Rudras, Nīlalohita; you are the Self of all beings, and by the Sāṅkhyas you are called Puruṣa. ॥42॥
2.4.12.43: Among mountains you are Sumeru, among the stars the moon; among the sages you are Vasiṣṭha, and likewise among the gods Vāsava (Indra). ॥43॥
2.4.12.44: You are the Oṃkāra of all the Vedas; be our protector, O Maheśvara. And for the welfare of the worlds you sprinkle (nourish) the beings. ॥44॥
2.4.12.45: O Maheśvara, O most fortunate one, observer of good and evil, O lord of gods, nourish us, who are indeed the doers of your word. ॥45॥
2.4.12.46: Among your thousands of crores of forms and hundreds of crores of forms, we are unable to reach the end; O god of gods, salutation be to you. ॥46॥
2.4.12.47: Brahmā said: Having thus praised him, all the gods headed by Viṣṇu, standing in front, bowed again and again, placing Skanda at their head. ॥47॥
2.4.12.48: Having heard the gods' hymn, Śiva, lord of all, the self-ruling one, became very pleased, and then, full of compassion, he smiled. ॥48॥
2.4.12.49: With a delighted mind, Śaṅkara, the supreme lord, friend of the afflicted and refuge of the good, spoke to Viṣṇu and the other best of gods. ॥49॥
2.4.12.50: Śiva said: O Hari, O Vidhi (Brahmā), O gods, listen to my words with attention. I am in every way the protector of the good, and for you gods, a treasure of compassion. ॥50॥
2.4.12.51: I am Śaṅkara, slayer of the wicked, lord of the three worlds, loving to devotees; creator, sustainer and destroyer of all, yet free from change. ॥51॥
2.4.12.52: Whenever distress befalls you, O best of gods, then you should worship me for the sake of your happiness. ॥52॥
2.4.12.53: Brahmā said: Thus commanded, the gods headed by Viṣṇu, together with the lords of sages, joyfully bowed to Śivā, to Śiva with her, and to Kumāra; ॥53॥
2.4.12.54: And recounting that delightful glory of Śiva and Śivā and of Śiva's son, having attained supreme bliss, they went to their own abodes, O sage. ॥54॥
2.4.12.55: Śiva too, the supreme lord, together with Śivā and his gaṇas, joined by Kumāra, dwelt joyfully and lovingly on that mountain. ॥55॥
2.4.12.56: Thus, O sage, the whole story of Kumāra has been told, which is Śaiva, bliss-giving and divine. What else do you wish to hear? ॥56॥
2.4.12.iti: Thus ends the twelfth adhyāya, named The deeds of Śiva and Śivā, containing the deeds of Lord Kārttika, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥12॥
2.4.13.1: Sūta said: Having heard this wonderful and excellent account of the enemy of Tāraka, Nārada was greatly pleased, and then he lovingly questioned Vidhi (Brahmā). ॥1॥
2.4.13.2: Nārada said: O god of gods, lord of creatures, treasury of the knowledge of Śiva, I have heard the noble story of Kārttika, which is finer even than nectar. ॥2॥
2.4.13.3: Now I wish to hear the excellent story of Gaṇeśa — the divine account of his birth, the most auspicious of all auspicious things. ॥3॥
2.4.13.4: Sūta said: Hearing these words of the great sage Nārada, Brahmā, pleased at heart, replied while remembering Śiva. ॥4॥
2.4.13.5: Brahmā said: Owing to the difference of kalpas, the birth of Gaṇeśa has been told in another way on higher authority: there his head, looked upon by Śani, was cut off, and an elephant's face was joined to him. ॥5॥
2.4.13.6: Now the origin of Gaṇeśa as told in the Śveta kalpa is narrated, in which his head was cut off by the compassionate Śiva. ॥6॥
2.4.13.7: No doubt should be entertained here, O sage: Śaṅkara is the maker of creation. That Śambhu is indeed the lord of all, without qualities and yet also with qualities. ॥7॥
2.4.13.8: By his play the whole universe is created, likewise sustained, and destroyed, O best of sages. Now listen attentively to the matter at hand. ॥8॥
2.4.13.9: After Śiva had been married and had gone to Kailāsa, within some time the birth of Gaṇapati took place. ॥9॥
2.4.13.10: At one time the friends Jayā and Vijayā, meeting together with Pārvatī, became engaged in deliberation. ॥10॥
2.4.13.11: They said: All the gaṇas belong to Rudra and are devoted to Śiva's command; all of them, headed by Nandin and Bhṛṅgin, are reckoned ours as well. ॥11॥
2.4.13.12: Those pramathas are countless, yet not one is our own. They all stand at the door, devoted to Śaṅkara's command. ॥12॥
2.4.13.13: Though all of them are ours too, still our mind does not accord with them. One who is truly our own should be created by you, O sinless one. ॥13॥
2.4.13.14: Brahmā said: When these beautiful words were spoken by her two friends, the goddess Pārvatī then considered them beneficial and resolved to carry them out. ॥14॥
2.4.13.15: Then once, while Pārvatī was bathing, Sadāśiva rebuked Nandin and came into the inner apartment. ॥15॥
2.4.13.16: Seeing Śaṅkara arriving at an untimely moment, the beautiful mother of the world, who was bathing, rose up then, embarrassed. ॥16॥
2.4.13.17: On that occasion the goddess, filled with eagerness, considered the words of her friends beneficial and conducive to happiness. ॥17॥
2.4.13.18: When things had happened thus, at some time Pārvatī Śivā, the supreme goddess possessing the highest māyā, reflected in her mind as follows: ॥18॥
2.4.13.19: Let there be some servant of my own, very auspicious and capable, who will not move even a line's breadth from my command. ॥19॥
2.4.13.20: Having reflected thus, the goddess created from the dirt of her body a person endowed with all auspicious marks, ॥20॥
2.4.13.21: flawless in all his limbs, beautiful in all his limbs, large, rich in every splendour, of great strength and valour. ॥21॥
2.4.13.22: Then she gave him various garments, many kinds of ornaments, and abundant, unsurpassed blessings. ॥22॥
2.4.13.23: You are my son, you are my own; I have no one else here. Thus addressed, that person bowed to Śivā and spoke. ॥23॥
2.4.13.24: Gaṇeśa said: What task do you have today? I shall do what you command. Thus addressed by him, Śivā then replied to her son. ॥24॥
2.4.13.25: Śivā said: O dear one, hear my word: be my doorkeeper today. You are my son, you are my own; I have no one else. ॥25॥
2.4.13.26: Without my permission, good son, no one at all, from anywhere, may force his way into my inner apartment, dear one. This I have spoken truly. ॥26॥
2.4.13.27: Brahmā said: Having said this, O sage, she gave him a very strong staff, and looking at his beautiful form she was filled with joy. ॥27॥
2.4.13.28: Kissing his face and embracing her son with great love and tenderness, she stationed the lord of gaṇas, staff in hand, at her door. ॥28॥
2.4.13.29: Then, dear one, the goddess's son, the gaṇa, a great hero, staff in hand, stood at the door of the house, wishing for Pārvatī's good. ॥29॥
2.4.13.30: Having stationed Gaṇeśa, her own son, at her door, Śivā herself remained bathing, accompanied by her friends. ॥30॥
2.4.13.31: At that very moment Śiva arrived at the door, playful, O tiger among sages, skilled in many sports. ॥31॥
2.4.13.32: Not recognising that lord Śiva, the lord of gaṇas said: O god, without my mother's permission you may not go in now. ॥32॥
2.4.13.33: My mother is engaged in bathing. Where are you going? Go away from here now. Saying this, he then seized his staff to block him. ॥33॥
2.4.13.34: Seeing him, Śiva said: Whom are you forbidding, foolish one? Do you not know me, wicked-minded one? I am Śiva, none other. ॥34॥
2.4.13.35: Struck with the staff by Gaṇeśa, Maheśvara, who delights in many sports, grew angry and replied to that son. ॥35॥
2.4.13.36: Śiva said: You are a fool, you do not know: I am Śiva, the husband of Girijā. I am going into my own house, boy — how can you stop me? ॥36॥
2.4.13.37: Brahmā said: As Maheśa, having said this, was entering, the leader of the gaṇas grew angry, O brahmin, and struck him again with the staff. ॥37॥
2.4.13.38: Then Śiva, enraged, commanded his own gaṇas: Who is this standing here, and what is he doing? Look into it, O gaṇas. ॥38॥
2.4.13.39: Having said this, Śiva stood there outside the house in anger — the Lord who delights in worldly conduct and performs many wondrous sports. ॥39॥
2.4.13.iti: Thus ends the thirteenth adhyāya, named The birth of Gaṇeśa, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥13॥
2.4.14.1: Brahmā said: Those gaṇas, filled with anger, went there at Śiva's command and then questioned that son of Girijā, the gatekeeper. ॥1॥
2.4.14.2: The attendants of Śiva said: Who are you? Where have you come from? And what do you intend to do? Go far away from here today, if you wish to live. ॥2॥
2.4.14.3: Brahmā said: Hearing those words of theirs, that son of Girijā, fearless and staff in hand, said this to the would-be gatekeepers. ॥3॥
2.4.14.4: Gaṇeśa said: Who are you, and where have you come from, you handsome ones here? Go far away. Why are you standing here as opponents? ॥4॥
2.4.14.5: Brahmā said: Hearing his words thus and laughing among themselves, all the gaṇas of Śiva, great heroes, now unabashed, spoke. ॥5॥
2.4.14.6: Having spoken thus to one another, all those attendants of Śiva, angry at heart, replied to that gatekeeper Gaṇeśa. ॥6॥
2.4.14.7: The attendants of Śiva said: Listen: we are indeed the gatekeepers, the foremost gaṇas of Śiva. We have come to stop you by the command of the Lord Śaṅkara. ॥7॥
2.4.14.8: Considering you too to be a gaṇa here, we do not kill you; otherwise you would be slain. Keep far away of your own accord—why do you seek death? ॥8॥
2.4.14.9: Brahmā said: Though addressed thus, Gaṇeśa, the fearless son of Girijā, rebuked Śaṅkara's gaṇas and did not then give up the door. ॥9॥
2.4.14.10: All those gaṇas of Śiva who were there, having heard his words, then went to Śiva and told him what had happened. ॥10॥
2.4.14.11: Then, hearing their report, Maheśvara of wondrous play, the goal of the worlds, rebuked his own gaṇas and spoke, O sage. ॥11॥
2.4.14.12: Maheśvara said: Who is this fellow, and what does he say, puffed up like an enemy? What will this ill-minded one do? Surely he desires his own death. ॥12॥
2.4.14.13: Let this new gatekeeper be driven far away. How is it that you stand there like eunuchs and report his doings to me? ॥13॥
2.4.14.14: Told thus by their master Śambhu of wondrous play, those gaṇas came back to that very spot and spoke to the gatekeeper. ॥14॥
2.4.14.15: The attendants of Śiva said: Hey, hey, door-guard, who are you, standing here? By whom were you posted? You take no account of us at all—how then do you wish to live? ॥15॥
2.4.14.16: We are all standing here as the gatekeepers; why do you bluster? A jackal that has seized a lion's seat merely hopes for its own safety. ॥16॥
2.4.14.17: You roar, fool, only so long as the might of the gaṇas has not been felt by you; once it is felt, you will fall right here. ॥17॥
2.4.14.18: Addressed thus by them, he grew very angry, and then, seizing his staff with both hands, he struck those gaṇas who were speaking insolently. ॥18॥
2.4.14.19: Then the son of Śivā, the fearless lord of gaṇas, rebuking those great heroes, the chief gaṇas of Śaṅkara, spoke. ॥19॥
2.4.14.20: The son of Śivā said: Go, go far away from here. If not, I will show you my own exceedingly fierce valour, and you will become utter laughing-stocks. ॥20॥
2.4.14.21: Hearing those words of Girijā's son, Śaṅkara's gaṇas then spoke among themselves. ॥21॥
2.4.14.22: The attendants of Śiva said: What should be done? Where should we go? Why is he not dealt with? We are keeping to propriety; otherwise what could he say? ॥22॥
2.4.14.23: Brahmā said: Then all Śambhu's gaṇas went to Śiva, who was staying at a distance, a mere krośa from Kailāsa, and told him likewise. ॥23॥
2.4.14.24: Śiva, the Supreme Lord, trident in hand and fierce of mind, laughed and spoke to all those gaṇas of his, who were esteemed as heroes. ॥24॥
2.4.14.25: Śiva said: Hey, hey, gaṇas, you have the minds of eunuchs; you are no heroes, only thinking yourselves heroes. You are not fit to speak before me. Rebuked by him, what more can one say? ॥25॥
2.4.14.26: Go, and let him be beaten, whoever he may be who holds sway here. What use is much talk on this? He must simply be removed. ॥26॥
2.4.14.27: Brahmā said: Thus rebuked by Maheśa, that god, all those best of gaṇas went there, O lord of sages, and spoke. ॥27॥
2.4.14.28: The attendants of Śiva said: Hey, you, listen, boy. Why do you talk so insolently, relying on force? Go far away from here; if not, death will be yours. ॥28॥
2.4.14.29: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of those who were surely carrying out Śiva's command, the son of Śivā became distressed then, thinking, what shall I do? ॥29॥
2.4.14.30: Meanwhile the Goddess, hearing again the quarrel at the door between them and him, said to her friend, go and see. ॥30॥
2.4.14.31: The friend came there and understood what had happened; having watched for a moment, she went back delighted to Śivā's presence. ॥31॥
2.4.14.32: Having gone there, O sage, that friend related in full before Girijā everything that had happened. ॥32॥
2.4.14.33: The friend said: O Great Goddess, that gaṇa of ours who stands at the door—Śaṅkara's heroic gaṇas are surely abusing him. ॥33॥
2.4.14.34: How can Śiva and all the gaṇas force their way into the house without your leave? This is not good for you. ॥34॥
2.4.14.35: He has acted rightly indeed, for no one has been let in, even though he has suffered pain here, as well as insult and the like. ॥35॥
2.4.14.36: From now on, a war of words is going on between them. Even when the dispute has taken place, let them not simply come in at their ease. ॥36॥
2.4.14.37: Since the dispute has been started here, let them all enter only by defeating him and winning; never otherwise, my dear. ॥37॥
2.4.14.38: In this very one of ours, all of us have been insulted. Therefore, O Goddess, O gracious one, you must not give up your high self-respect. ॥38॥
2.4.14.39: Śiva today always behaves toward you like a monkey, O virtuous lady. What arrogance will he show? He will become compliant. ॥39॥
2.4.14.40: Brahmā said: Ah! Satī remained there for a moment, under the sway of Śiva's will. ॥40॥
2.4.14.41: Then Pārvatī, becoming proud and resolute, spoke within her mind: ॥41॥
2.4.14.42: Śivā said: Ah! He (Śiva) did not wait even for a moment; how was this forcible entry made? And how should I act here now — with humility, or otherwise? ॥42॥
2.4.14.43: What is to happen will surely happen; what has been done cannot be otherwise. Having said this, the beloved Pārvatī then sent a female companion there. ॥43॥
2.4.14.44: She came and spoke what the beloved Pārvatī had told her; she then reported it to Gaṇeśa, the son of Girijā. ॥44॥
2.4.14.45: The friend said: You have done well, good one; let them not enter by force. How can these gaṇas, standing before you, conquer one such as you? ॥45॥
2.4.14.46: Whether it has been done or not done, you must do what is to be done. Whoever is defeated, again — there is surely no enmity in it. ॥46॥
2.4.14.47: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of her and of his mother, the lord of gaṇas attained supreme joy, abundant strength and great exaltation. ॥47॥
2.4.14.48: Girding his loins and tying on his turban, touching his shanks and thighs, he joyfully spoke fearless words to all those gaṇas. ॥48॥
2.4.14.49: Gaṇeśa said: I am the son of Girijā, and you are Śiva's gaṇas; both of us stand on equal footing, so let what must be done be done. ॥49॥
2.4.14.50: You are doorkeepers; why am I not a doorkeeper too? You are stationed there, and I am stationed here — that is settled. ॥50॥
2.4.14.51: When it is settled that you are stationed here, then you should carry out Śiva's command. ॥51॥
2.4.14.52: But now, O heroes, it is I who am here truly carrying out Śivā's command; I have decided this as is fitting. ॥52॥
2.4.14.53: Therefore, all you gaṇas of Śiva, listen attentively to my word: neither by force nor by entreaty shall you go into the palace again. ॥53॥
2.4.14.54: Brahmā said: Thus addressed by the gaṇa Gaṇeśa, all those gaṇas, ashamed, went to Śiva; having bowed, they stood before him. ॥54॥
2.4.14.55: Standing there, they all reported that astonishing account; with joined palms and bowed shoulders, having praised Śiva, they stood before him. ॥55॥
2.4.14.56: Then, having heard all that account told by his own gaṇas, Śaṅkara, adopting worldly conduct, spoke these words. ॥56॥
2.4.14.57: Śaṅkara said: Listen, all you gaṇas: a fight would not be proper, for you here are mine, and he likewise is Gaurī's gaṇa. ॥57॥
2.4.14.58: Yet if humility is shown, the report will spread in the world that Śambhu is always under his wife's control; my gaṇas would surely be reproached. ॥58॥
2.4.14.59: When something has been done, one must respond in kind — this is the weightier policy. That gaṇa is a lone boy; what valour can he show? ॥59॥
2.4.14.60: You gaṇas are renowned in the world and highly skilled in battle. Being mine, how could you abandon the fight and go into disgrace? ॥60॥
2.4.14.61: How can a woman be obstinate, especially before her husband? Having done so, Girijā will surely reap its fruit. ॥61॥
2.4.14.62: Therefore, all my heroes, listen attentively to my word: you must fight by all means; let whatever is to be, be. ॥62॥
2.4.14.63: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, O Brahmin, Śaṅkara, skilled in many sportive plays, fell silent, O best of sages, displaying the way of the world. ॥63॥
2.4.14.iti: Thus ends the fourteenth adhyāya, named The dispute of the gaṇas, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥14॥
2.4.15.1: Brahmā said: Thus addressed by that Lord, they came to a firm resolve; then, armed for battle, they went there to Śiva's abode. ॥1॥
2.4.15.2: Gaṇeśa too, seeing the excellent gaṇas thus arrived, and making a show of readiness for battle, said this to them as they stood there. ॥2॥
2.4.15.3: Gaṇeśa said: Let all the gaṇa-leaders come, who carry out Śiva's command. I am alone, and a boy, carrying out Śivā's (Pārvatī's) command. ॥3॥
2.4.15.4: Even so, let the goddess Pārvatī see the strength of her son, and let Śiva in turn see the strength of his own gaṇas. ॥4॥
2.4.15.5: This will be a battle between the mighty and a boy, between the sides of Bhavānī and Śiva. You, skilled in warfare, have fought battles before; ॥5॥
2.4.15.6: by me it was never done before; I am a boy, yet it is being done now. Even so, the shame here before Girijā and Śiva will be yours. ॥6॥
2.4.15.7: It will not be so for me; the reverse will happen. The shame here before Girijā and Śiva will be yours, not mine. ॥7॥
2.4.15.8: Knowing this, O lords of the gaṇas, the battle must be fought—by you with an eye to your master, and by me with an eye to my mother. ॥8॥
2.4.15.9: Whatever kind of battle is fought, let what must be, be. No one in the three worlds is able to prevent it. ॥9॥
2.4.15.10: Brahmā said: Thus rebuked, they, their arms adorned with staffs, took up various weapons and advanced together. ॥10॥
2.4.15.11: Grinding their teeth and roaring huṃ again and again, crying, look, look, those gaṇas drew near. ॥11॥
2.4.15.12: Nandī, coming first, seized a foot and pulled; Bhṛṅgī, running up, seized the gaṇa's other foot. ॥12॥
2.4.15.13: While the two were pulling at his feet, the gaṇa struck them on their hands with his hand, and himself freed his two feet from them. ॥13॥
2.4.15.14: Then the heroic son of the Goddess, Gaṇapati, standing at the door, seized a huge iron club and struck down all of them. ॥14॥
2.4.15.15: Of some the hands were broken, of some the backs, of some the heads, and of some the skulls. ॥15॥
2.4.15.16: Of some the knees there, of some the shoulders likewise were broken. All those who came face to face with him were struck in the chest. ॥16॥
2.4.15.17: Some fell to the ground, some fled to the intermediate quarters, of some both feet were severed, and some went to Śarva. ॥17॥
2.4.15.18: Among them not one stood facing him in the fight; just as deer, seeing a lion, flee in the ten directions, ॥18॥
2.4.15.19: so all those gaṇas fled by the thousands. And he too, turning back, took his stand at the fine doorway. ॥19॥
2.4.15.20: Just as Kāla (Time/Death) appears terrifying when bringing about the end of an aeon, so he appeared, as the bringer of dissolution to all. ॥20॥
2.4.15.21: At this very time all the gods, together with the lord of Ramā (Viṣṇu) and the lord of the gods (Indra), urged by Nārada, assembled here. ॥21॥
2.4.15.22: Then all of them, wishing Śiva's good, stood before him, bowed to Śiva and said: Give us your command, O Lord. ॥22॥
2.4.15.23: You are the supreme Brahman, the lord of all, and all are your servants; you are the creator of the world, ever its sustainer and destroyer, the supreme Lord. ॥23॥
2.4.15.24: Through sport you take the forms of rajas, sattva and tamas, while by nature you are beyond attributes. What sport have you devised today? Tell us that now, O Lord. ॥24॥
2.4.15.25: Brahmā said: Hearing their words, O best of sages, Maheśvara, seeing then his gaṇas shattered, related everything to them. ॥25॥
2.4.15.26: Then Śaṅkara, lord of all and lord of Girijā, O best of sages, laughed and spoke to me, Brahmā. ॥26॥
2.4.15.27: Śiva said: Listen, Brahmā: at my door stands a single boy, very mighty, staff in hand, barring entry into the house. ॥27॥
2.4.15.28: He deals mighty blows and strikes down my attendants; by force he has inflicted defeat on my gaṇas here. ॥28॥
2.4.15.29: Brahmā, you yourself must go; this mighty one must be pacified. O Vidhi, act so that conciliation may come about. ॥29॥
2.4.15.30: Brahmā said: Hearing the Lord's words, not understanding, deluded by ignorance, I went near him, dear one, with all the foremost sages. ॥30॥
2.4.15.31: Seeing me approach, that very mighty Gaṇeśa grew angry, rushed up, and plucked out my beard. ॥31॥
2.4.15.32: Forgive me, forgive me, O god. I have not come to fight. I am a brāhmaṇa, deserving favour, a maker of peace, harmless. ॥32॥
2.4.15.33: While I was speaking thus, O brāhmaṇa, that Gaṇeśa, the great hero, a boy of more than boyish valour, took up the iron club. ॥33॥
2.4.15.34: Seeing that mighty Gaṇeśa with the club in hand, I, bent on flight, then ran off very swiftly. ॥34॥
2.4.15.35: Crying, go, go, they were then struck by the club; some fell by themselves, and some were felled by him. ॥35॥
2.4.15.36: And some, reaching Śiva's presence in that very instant, reported the whole event to Śiva. ॥36॥
2.4.15.37: Seeing them in such a state and hearing that account, Hara, skilled in divine sport, conceived boundless anger. ॥37॥
2.4.15.38: He then commanded all the hosts of gods headed by Indra, the gaṇas led by Ṣaṇmukha, and the bhūtas, pretas and piśācas. ॥38॥
2.4.15.39: All of them, as befitted each, went forth from every direction, eager to kill that gaṇa, commanded by Śiva, with weapons raised. ॥39॥
2.4.15.40: Whatever weapon each one had, all of it in particular, rushing up with force, they hurled upon Gaṇeśa. ॥40॥
2.4.15.41: A great cry of distress arose in the three worlds with their moving and unmoving beings; all the people dwelling in the three worlds fell into the utmost anxiety. ॥41॥
2.4.15.42: They thought: Even Brahmā's lifespan has not run out, yet the cosmic egg is surely going to destruction — untimely indeed, by the force of Śiva's own will. ॥42॥
2.4.15.43: All those who had come there, and those again headed by Ṣaṇmukha — the gods, their weapons rendered futile, were struck with supreme amazement. ॥43॥
2.4.15.44: Meanwhile the goddess Jagadambā, the awakener of all, having learned of all that had been done, conceived boundless anger. ॥44॥
2.4.15.45: Then, O lord of sages, two Śaktis were created there by that goddess, for the purpose of giving every help to her own gaṇa. ॥45॥
2.4.15.46: One of them, O great sage, assuming a fierce form, stood there, opening wide her cave-like mouth, resembling a dark mountain. ॥46॥
2.4.15.47: The other had the form of lightning, was endowed with many arms — a terrifying great goddess, dealing punishment to the wicked. ॥47॥
2.4.15.48: All the weapons released by the gods and gaṇas, the two seized in their mouths and swiftly hurled back. ॥48॥
2.4.15.49: No weapon of the gods could be seen — only the iron club of Gaṇeśa all around again. Thus a most wondrous deed was performed there by the two. ॥49॥
2.4.15.50: A single boy churned up the entire invincible army, just as the ocean was churned of old by the best of mountains. ॥50॥
2.4.15.51: All the immortals headed by Śakra were struck down by him alone, and Śaṅkara's gaṇas too then became distraught. ॥51॥
2.4.15.52: Then all of them, gathering together and sighing again and again, distressed by his blows, spoke to one another. ॥52॥
2.4.15.53: The hosts of the gods said: What should be done? Where should we go? The ten directions cannot be made out. He whirls his club to the left and to the right. ॥53॥
2.4.15.54: Brahmā said: At this time the foremost apsarases, with flowers and sandal-paste in their hands, and the sages headed by you, who were exceedingly eager for a great battle — ॥54॥
2.4.15.55: — they all came together to witness the battle; and then, O best of sages, the fair pathway of the sky was filled with them. ॥55॥
2.4.15.56: Those apsarases and those sages, seeing that battle, were filled with great wonder, for such a supreme battle had never been seen even once. ॥56॥
2.4.15.57: Then the earth together with the oceans trembled there, and the mountains fell; all this upheaval was brought about by the battle. ॥57॥
2.4.15.58: The sky reeled with its hosts of planets and stars; all became agitated. All the gods then fled, and all the gaṇas as well. ॥58॥
2.4.15.59: Only the valiant Ṣaṇmukha did not flee there; the great hero, holding them all back, stood in front. ॥59॥
2.4.15.60: In that battle all were rendered fruitless by the two Śaktis; all the missiles hurled by the immortals and gaṇas were cut to pieces. ॥60॥
2.4.15.61: Those who remained all came into Śiva's presence — all the gods who had fled, and all the gaṇas too, then. ॥61॥
2.4.15.62: Gathered together, they bowed to Śiva again and again and quickly said: Who is this excellent gaṇa, O Lord? ॥62॥
2.4.15.63: Battles have been heard of before, and now again many are seen; but such a one was never heard of or seen at any time. ॥63॥
2.4.15.64: Let something be considered, O God; otherwise there will be no victory. You alone, O Master, are the protector of the universe — there is no doubt. ॥64॥
2.4.15.65: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of theirs, Rudra, who is fierce in wrath, grew angry and went right there with his own gaṇas. ॥65॥
2.4.15.66: And that whole army of the gods, together with Viṣṇu the discus-bearer, making a great festive display, followed Śiva. ॥66॥
2.4.15.67: Meanwhile, O Nārada, you bowed with devotion to Maheśvara and, with folded hands, addressed the God of gods. ॥67॥
2.4.15.68: Nārada said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, hear my words, O all-pervading one. You alone are the omnipresent Master, skilled in manifold sports. ॥68॥
2.4.15.69: By performing a great sport, you have removed the pride of the gaṇas, and, by granting abundant strength to this one, the pride of the gods as well, O Śaṅkara. ॥69॥
2.4.15.70: Your own wondrous strength has been displayed in the world, O Lord, by you, the independent one, the destroyer of all pride, O Śambhu. ॥70॥
2.4.15.71: Now, O Lord, loving to your devotees, do not prolong that sport; honour your own gaṇas and the immortals well and make them prosper. ॥71॥
2.4.15.72: Do not play with him any longer now; slay him, O bestower of the state of Brahman. Having said this, O Nārada, you then vanished. ॥72॥
2.4.15.iti: Thus ends the fifteenth adhyāya, named The battle of Gaṇeśa, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥15॥
2.4.16.1: Brahmā said: Having heard this, Maheśāna, who bestows grace on his devotees, became eager to fight that boy, O Nārada, at your word. ॥1॥
2.4.16.2: Having summoned Viṣṇu and taken counsel with him, the three-eyed god, accompanied by a great force and with the gods, came face to face with him. ॥2॥
2.4.16.3: And the gods fought with him, remembering Śiva's lotus feet — very strong, full of great zeal, beheld by Śiva's gracious glance. ॥3॥
2.4.16.4: Then Hari, of great strength and valour, fought with him — the hero bearing great divine weapons, devoted, himself a form of Śiva. ॥4॥
2.4.16.5: Then that lord of the gaṇas, the hero endowed with great strength granted by Śakti, suddenly struck the foremost of the gods and Hari with his staff. ॥5॥
2.4.16.6: All the hosts of gods there, O sage, had their strength blunted; struck by him with the staff, together with Viṣṇu, they turned their backs. ॥6॥
2.4.16.7: Śiva too, having fought for a long time with his army, O sage, and seeing him so formidable, was filled with the greatest astonishment. ॥7॥
2.4.16.8: He must be slain only by stratagem; otherwise he cannot be slain — settling on this thought, he took his stand in the midst of the army. ॥8॥
2.4.16.9: Then, when the god Śiva — attributeless yet taking form with attributes — was seen, and when Viṣṇu too had come to the battle, all the deities ॥9॥
2.4.16.10: and the gaṇas of Maheśa then attained great joy; all of them, meeting one another with affection, held a celebration. ॥10॥
2.4.16.11: Then the heroic son of Śakti, with a hero's stride, first honoured with his own staff Viṣṇu, the bringer of all happiness. ॥11॥
2.4.16.12: Viṣṇu said: I shall delude him, and let him be slain by you, O Lord. Without a stratagem he cannot be killed; he is of tāmasic nature and hard to overcome. ॥12॥
2.4.16.13: Having made up his mind thus and consulted thoroughly with Śambhu, Viṣṇu, receiving Śiva's command, set himself to deluding him. ॥13॥
2.4.16.14: The two Śaktis, seeing Hari engaged in this way, gave the power of Śakti to Gaṇeśa and merged into him, O sage. ॥14॥
2.4.16.15: Then, the two Śaktis having merged into him, Gaṇeśa, now even mightier, hurled his iron club to where Viṣṇu himself was standing. ॥15॥
2.4.16.16: Making some effort here, Viṣṇu evaded its course, remembering Śiva Maheśāna, his own lord, who is affectionate to devotees. ॥16॥
2.4.16.17: Seeing his face turned to one side, Śaṅkara too came, taking up his trident, greatly enraged, eager for battle. ॥17॥
2.4.16.18: The mighty hero, son of Śivā, saw Śambhu Maheśvara arrive, trident in hand, wishing to slay him. ॥18॥
2.4.16.19: Remembering his mother's lotus feet, that great hero Gaṇeśa, strengthened by Śiva's Śakti, struck him on the hand with a spear. ॥19॥
2.4.16.20: Seeing the trident fallen from his hand, Śiva, the Supreme Self, together with his attendants, took up the bow Pināka. ॥20॥
2.4.16.21: That too the lord of gaṇas knocked to the ground with his club. Thus five of Śiva's hands were struck; with the other five he took up the trident. ॥21॥
2.4.16.22: Alas, surely a more grievous trouble has now arisen for me! What could befall the gaṇas again? So spoke Bhava, following worldly ways. ॥22॥
2.4.16.23: Meanwhile the heroic lord of gaṇas, endowed with strength given by Śakti, struck the gods along with the gaṇas with his club. ॥23॥
2.4.16.24: The gods with the gaṇas, battered by the club, fled to the ten directions; none could stand in battle against that wondrous striker. ॥24॥
2.4.16.25: Viṣṇu, seeing that gaṇa, said: Blessed is he — of great strength, a great hero, very valiant, delighting in battle. ॥25॥
2.4.16.26: Many deities have I seen, and likewise many Dānavas, Daityas, Yakṣas, Gandharvas and Rākṣasas, ॥26॥
2.4.16.27: but none of them in all the three worlds attains equality with this lord of gaṇas in splendour, beauty, valour, virtues and the like. ॥27॥
2.4.16.28: As he was speaking thus, the son of Śakti, lord of gaṇas, whirling his club, hurled it there at Viṣṇu. ॥28॥
2.4.16.29: Hari took up his discus, remembering Śiva's lotus feet, and with that discus the club was quickly shattered to pieces. ॥29॥
2.4.16.30: The gaṇa hurled a fragment of the club at Hari; it was caught by the bird Garuḍa and rendered futile. ॥30॥
2.4.16.31: Thus for a long time both great heroes, Viṣṇu and the gaṇa, fought with each other. ॥31॥
2.4.16.32: Again the best of heroes, the mighty son of Śakti, remembering Śiva, took up his matchless staff and struck Viṣṇu with it. ॥32॥
2.4.16.33: Unable to bear that blow, he fell to the ground; rising quickly, he fought on with that son of Śivā. ॥33॥
2.4.16.34: Seizing this opportunity, the trident-bearer came from the north and cut off his head with the trident. ॥34॥
2.4.16.35: When the head of that lord of gaṇas was cut off, O Nārada, the army of the gaṇas and the army of the gods became utterly still. ॥35॥
2.4.16.36: You, Nārada, came and reported everything to the Goddess: O proud lady, listen — you must not give up your pride now. ॥36॥
2.4.16.37: Having said this, you, Nārada, lover of strife, vanished from there — you, the sage ever unchanging, who carry out the intent of Śambhu. ॥37॥
2.4.16.iti: Thus ends the sixteenth adhyāya, named The battle of Gaṇeśa and the cutting off of his head, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥16॥
2.4.17.1: Nārada said: O Brahmā, O greatly wise one, tell me: now that I have heard that whole account, what did the great Goddess do next? I wish to hear it truly. ॥1॥
2.4.17.2: Brahmā said: Listen, O tiger among sages; today I shall surely narrate the deeds of the Mother of the world that took place after that. ॥2॥
2.4.17.3: The Gaṇas then beat mṛdaṅga drums and kettle-drums, and held a great festival when that lord of the Gaṇas had been slain. ॥3॥
2.4.17.4: Even as Śiva, having cut off his head, was seized with grief, at that very time the goddess Girijā became exceedingly angry, O lord of sages. ॥4॥
2.4.17.5: She said: What shall I do? Where shall I go? Alas, alas, sorrow has befallen me! How can this sorrow be destroyed? Great is my anguish now. ॥5॥
2.4.17.6: My son has been destroyed today by all the gods and the Gaṇas. I shall destroy them all, or I shall bring about the dissolution of the world. ॥6॥
2.4.17.7: Grieving thus, she, the great Sovereign of all worlds, in her wrath instantly created Śaktis by hundreds of thousands. ॥7॥
2.4.17.8: Those Śaktis, once created, blazing with energy, bowed then to Śivā, the Mother of the world, and said: O Mother, command us. ॥8॥
2.4.17.9: Hearing that, she—Śambhu's Śakti, Prakṛti, Mahāmāyā—intent on wrath, replied to all of them, O lord of sages. ॥9॥
2.4.17.10: The Goddess said: O Śaktis, O goddesses, now by my command you must bring about dissolution here; there should be no hesitation in this. ॥10॥
2.4.17.11: O friends, forcibly devour the gods, the sages, the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas, both our own people and others. ॥11॥
2.4.17.12: Brahmā said: Thus commanded, all those Śaktis, intent on wrath, set about destroying the gods and all the rest. ॥12॥
2.4.17.13: Just as fire destroys grass, so all those Śaktis set about the destruction. ॥13॥
2.4.17.14: Whether it was a leader of the Gaṇas, or Viṣṇu, or Brahmā, or Śaṅkara, or Indra, or the king of the Yakṣas, or Skanda, or even Sūrya— ॥14॥
2.4.17.15: —the Śaktis went on ceaselessly destroying them all; wherever anyone was seen, there the Śaktis were too. ॥15॥
2.4.17.16: Many of them—fearsome, hunchbacked, lame, long-headed—seized the gods in their hands and then flung them into their mouths. ॥16॥
2.4.17.17: Seeing that destruction then, Hara, Brahmā and Hari, all the gods headed by Indra, the Gaṇas and the sages likewise— ॥17॥
2.4.17.18: —fell into doubt: What will this goddess do? Will she bring about an untimely dissolution? And their hope of life was lost. ॥18॥
2.4.17.19: All of them gathered together: Let it be considered what is to be done. Deliberating thus, they quickly spoke to one another. ॥19॥
2.4.17.20: Only when the goddess Girijā becomes gracious here will there be well-being; not otherwise, even with countless efforts. ॥20॥
2.4.17.21: Śiva too, expert in manifold divine play, fell into grief, adopting the ways of the world and deluding everyone there. ॥21॥
2.4.17.22: When the backs of all the gods had been broken, then no one dared to go before Śivā, who was wrath incarnate. ॥22॥
2.4.17.23: Whether one's own or another's, god or demon, Gaṇa or guardian of a quarter, Yakṣa, Kinnara or sage, ॥23॥
2.4.17.24: or Viṣṇu, or Brahmā, or the Lord Śaṅkara himself—no one was able to stand before Girijā, O sage. ॥24॥
2.4.17.25: Seeing that blazing radiance burning on all sides, they all became exceedingly afraid and stood very far away. ॥25॥
2.4.17.26: At that time, O sage, you, Nārada of divine vision, arrived there for the comfort of the hosts of gods. ॥26॥
2.4.17.27: He bowed to me, Brahmā, to Bhava, to Viṣṇu and to Śaṅkara, and coming together and meeting them, spoke, considering what was to be done. ॥27॥
2.4.17.28: All the gods consulted together with you, the great-souled one, on how the distress might be allayed; then they said together: ॥28॥
2.4.17.29: As long as the goddess Girijā does not show mercy, there will be no happiness at all; of this there is no doubt. ॥29॥
2.4.17.30: Then the sages, with you at their head, went to Śivā's presence, and all of them sought to propitiate Śivā to calm her wrath. ॥30॥
2.4.17.31: Again and again they bowed, praising her with many hymns; propitiating her with love, all of them spoke at the behest of the hosts of gods. ॥31॥
2.4.17.32: The divine sages said: O Mother of the world, salutation to you. Salutation be to you, Śivā. Salutation to you, Caṇḍikā; and salutation be to you, Kalyāṇī. ॥32॥
2.4.17.33: You alone, O Mother, are the primordial Śakti, ever the maker of all creation; you alone are the sustaining power, and you alone bring about dissolution. ॥33॥
2.4.17.34: Be gracious, O Sovereign of the gods; bring peace — salutation to you. For the whole of the three worlds is distressed by your anger, O Goddess. ॥34॥
2.4.17.35: Brahmā said: Though praised thus by the sages headed by you, the supreme Goddess Śivā, looking at them with an angry glance, said nothing at all. ॥35॥
2.4.17.36: Then all the sages, bowing at her lotus feet, again spoke softly to Śivā with devotion, their palms joined. ॥36॥
2.4.17.37: Forgive, forgive, O Goddess. Destruction is happening now. Your Lord is standing here—look, look at him, O Ambikā. ॥37॥
2.4.17.38: Who are we? And these gods, Viṣṇu, Brahmā and the rest, are your own subjects, standing with palms joined. ॥38॥
2.4.17.39: The offence of all must be forgiven, O Supreme Sovereign. All are distressed today; grant them peace, O Śivā. ॥39॥
2.4.17.40: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, all the sages, utterly wretched and agitated, then stood before Caṇḍikā with palms joined. ॥40॥
2.4.17.41: Hearing their words in this way, Caṇḍikā became pleased, and with her mind filled with compassion she replied to those sages. ॥41॥
2.4.17.42: The Goddess said: If my son comes back to life, then there will be no destruction; and only if he becomes worthy of worship among you all — ॥42॥
2.4.17.43: and if he becomes the chief of all today — if you bring that about, then there will be peace in the world; otherwise you will not attain happiness. ॥43॥
2.4.17.44: Brahmā said: Thus addressed, all those sages, beginning with you, then came to those gods and reported everything that had happened. ॥44॥
2.4.17.45: And all those gods, Śakra and the rest, having heard this, bowed with joined palms and, dejected, reported it to Śaṅkara. ॥45॥
2.4.17.46: Having heard the gods, Śiva too spoke thus in turn: It must be done in that way, so that the well-being of all the worlds may come about here. ॥46॥
2.4.17.47: Go again towards the north; whoever is met first there, bring back his head and join it to the body. ॥47॥
2.4.17.48: Brahmā said: Then they, carrying out Śiva's command, did all that: they brought the body and washed it according to rule, ॥48॥
2.4.17.49: and having worshipped it, they then went facing northward. There an elephant with a single tusk was the first to be met. ॥49॥
2.4.17.50: Then, taking its head, they firmly joined it there. Having joined it, all the deities bowed then to Śiva, Viṣṇu and Brahmā, ॥50॥
2.4.17.51: and bowing, they spoke these words: What you commanded has been done by us. What remains of the task after this is to be done by you, O Bhava. ॥51॥
2.4.17.52: Then the attendants and the gods shone forth happily; and having heard that word spoken by Śiva, they carried it out. ॥52॥
2.4.17.53: Then Brahmā, Viṣṇu and the gods there, bowing to the Lord Śiva, their own master, who is beyond the guṇas, spoke: ॥53॥
2.4.17.54: Since all of us were born from the splendour of you, the great-souled one, may that splendour of yours enter this body through the application of Vedic mantras. ॥54॥
2.4.17.55: With this invocation they consecrated excellent water, and, together remembering Śiva, they sprinkled it on that body. ॥55॥
2.4.17.56: By the mere touch of that water, the boy, endowed with consciousness, quickly came to life; and by Śiva's will he rose up as if from sleep. ॥56॥
2.4.17.57: He was handsome, exceedingly beautiful, elephant-faced, of a fine red hue, with a very cheerful face, radiant, and of charming form. ॥57॥
2.4.17.58: O lord of sages, seeing that boy, the son of Śivā, alive, all there rejoiced, and all sorrow came to an end. ॥58॥
2.4.17.59: All of them, filled with joy, showed him to the Goddess; seeing her son alive, the Goddess became overjoyed. ॥59॥
2.4.17.iti: Thus ends the seventeenth adhyāya, named Gaṇeśa restored to life, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥17॥
2.4.18.1: Nārada said: O lord of creatures, when Girijā's son had been revived and seen by the Goddess, what happened there after that? Kindly tell me that now. ॥1॥
2.4.18.2: Brahmā said: O lord of sages, hear now what took place when Girijā's son had been revived and seen by the Goddess; I shall tell you of that great festival. ॥2॥
2.4.18.3: O sage, Śivā's son, revived, untroubled and transformed with an elephant's head, the elephant-faced one, was then consecrated by the gods and the leaders of the gaṇas. ॥3॥
2.4.18.4: Seeing her son, the goddess Śivā, filled with joy, took the boy in her arms and embraced him with delight. ॥4॥
2.4.18.5: Then the Mother joyfully and lovingly gave various garments and many ornaments to Gaṇeśa, her own son. ॥5॥
2.4.18.6: Having been worshipped by that Goddess and by the Siddhis in many ways, he was then touched by her hand, which removes all sorrow. ॥6॥
2.4.18.7: Having worshipped her son and kissed his face, the Goddess, Śaṅkara's consort, then lovingly granted boons, saying: You have been made to suffer just now. ॥7॥
2.4.18.8: You are blessed, you have fulfilled your purpose; now be the first to be worshipped among all the immortals, always free from sorrow. ॥8॥
2.4.18.9: Since vermilion is now seen on your face, you shall therefore always be worshipped by men with vermilion. ॥9॥
2.4.18.10: Whoever performs your worship with flowers or sandal paste, with auspicious fragrance, with delightful food-offerings, with the waving of lights according to rule, ॥10॥
2.4.18.11: with betel, with gifts, with circumambulations, and with the rite of prostration — ॥11॥
2.4.18.12: for him there will indeed be complete success, no doubt; obstacles of many forms will undoubtedly be destroyed. ॥12॥
2.4.18.13: Brahmā said: Having said this, the great goddess Maheśvarī then worshipped her son again with many excellent articles. ॥13॥
2.4.18.14: Then, O brahmin, by Girijā's grace, well-being came to the gods and especially to the gaṇas in a mere instant. ॥14॥
2.4.18.15: At that moment the devoted gods led by Vāsava (Indra), having joyfully praised Śiva and propitiated that god, brought Gaṇeśa near Śiva. ॥15॥
2.4.18.16: Having approached Giriśa, they then placed that boy of Maheśānī on his lap, for the happiness of the three worlds. ॥16॥
2.4.18.17: Śiva too, placing his lotus-hand on his head, spoke these words to the gods: This is another son of mine. ॥17॥
2.4.18.18: Gaṇeśa too then rose, bowed to Śiva, bowed to Pārvatī, and likewise to me and to Viṣṇu, ॥18॥
2.4.18.19: and standing before Nārada and all the sages, he said: My offence should be forgiven; such pride is natural to men. ॥19॥
2.4.18.20: I, Śaṅkara and Viṣṇu — we three gods — replied together lovingly, granting him an excellent boon: ॥20॥
2.4.18.21: Just as we three chief gods are worshipped in the three worlds, so let this lord of the gaṇas be worshipped by all. ॥21॥
2.4.18.22: We are primordial, and he too is primordial and indeed worthy of worship; for Gaṇeśa is the remover of obstacles and the giver of the fruits of all desires. ॥22॥
2.4.18.23: Having first performed his worship, men should worship us afterwards. When we all are worshipped but he is not worshipped — ॥23॥
2.4.18.24: O gods, if worship of others is performed while he remains unworshipped, then its fruit is lost; there need be no deliberation about this. ॥24॥
2.4.18.25: Brahmā said: Having said this, that lord of the gaṇas was reverently worshipped first by Śiva with various articles, and afterwards worshipped by Viṣṇu. ॥25॥
2.4.18.26: He was worshipped there by me, Brahmā, and by Pārvatī, and by all the hosts of gods with supreme joy. ॥26॥
2.4.18.27: All, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Hara and the rest, gathering together right there, proclaimed Gaṇeśa the chief of all, for the satisfaction of Śivā. ॥27॥
2.4.18.28: And again Śiva, with a well-pleased mind, granted him many boons that bring happiness in the world forever. ॥28॥
2.4.18.29: Śiva said: O son of the daughter of the lord of mountains, I am pleased, no doubt. When I am pleased the world is pleased; no one can be hostile. ॥29॥
2.4.18.30: Since, though in the form of a child, you performed great valour, being Śakti's son and very radiant, therefore be ever happy. ॥30॥
2.4.18.31: May your name be foremost in destroying obstacles. Now become the chief of all my gaṇas, worthy of worship. ॥31॥
2.4.18.32: Having spoken thus, Śaṅkara at once performed many rites of worship and bestowed many blessings upon him. ॥32॥
2.4.18.33: Then the hosts of gods joyfully had song, instrumental music and dance performed, and so too the troupes of apsarases. ॥33॥
2.4.18.34: Once more a boon was given to that lord of the gaṇas by the well-pleased Śambhu, the great-souled Śiva himself. ॥34॥
2.4.18.35: O lord of the gaṇas, you were born on the fourth lunar day in the month of Bhādra, in the dark fortnight, at the auspicious time of moonrise. ॥35॥
2.4.18.36: In the first watch of the night your form became manifest from the noble-minded Girijā; hence your vow is supreme. ॥36॥
2.4.18.37: Therefore, beginning from that day, on that very lunar day, the most splendid vow should be joyfully observed, especially for the attainment of all success. ॥37॥
2.4.18.38: Until the fourth day comes round again at the end of the year, your vow should be observed by my command. ॥38॥
2.4.18.39: Those who desire incomparable and manifold happiness in worldly life should worship you with devotion on the fourth day according to rule. ॥39॥
2.4.18.40: Likewise, on the lovely fourth day in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, having bathed in the morning, one should then announce the vow to the brahmins. ॥40॥
2.4.18.41: Worship is to be done with dūrvā grass, and a fast of that kind is to be kept. When a watch (prahara) of the night has passed, a man should bathe and worship duly. ॥41॥
2.4.18.42: Having made an image of metal, or likewise one made of coral, or of white arka wood, or fashioned of clay, ॥42॥
2.4.18.43: having then installed it there, the man, self-restrained, should worship it here with various divine fragrances, sandal pastes and flowers. ॥43॥
2.4.18.44: The dūrvā should be a span long, three-jointed, and without root. With one hundred and one of such grass blades, ॥44॥
2.4.18.45: or with just twenty-one, he should worship the installed image, the leader of the gaṇas, with incense, lamps and various food offerings, ॥45॥
2.4.18.46: with betel and other fine articles of offering, prostrating and likewise with hymns. Having thus worshipped you there, he should also worship the crescent moon. ॥46॥
2.4.18.47: Afterwards, having honoured the brahmins, he should joyfully feed them with sweet foods; and then he himself should eat sweet food, without salt. ॥47॥
2.4.18.48: Then afterwards he should conclude all his own observances and remember Gaṇeśa; thus the auspicious vow becomes complete. ॥48॥
2.4.18.49: When a full year has thus passed with the vow, the man should then perform the rite of concluding (udyāpana) for the completion of the vow. ॥49॥
2.4.18.50: There, by my command, twelve brahmins are to be fed; and having set up a single pot, your image is to be worshipped. ॥50॥
2.4.18.51: Having then drawn an eight-petalled lotus on the altar according to Vedic rule, a homa is to be performed here by those free from stinginess with wealth. ॥51॥
2.4.18.52: Likewise here he should respectfully feed two women and two young boys, having worshipped them according to rule in front of the image. ॥52॥
2.4.18.53: A vigil is to be kept at night; in the morning he should worship again, and then perform the dismissal, praying for the deity's return. ॥53॥
2.4.18.54: Blessings are to be received from a boy, as well as the svastivācana; and he should offer a handful of flowers for the completion of the vow. ॥54॥
2.4.18.55: Then, having made obeisances, he should carry out the various remaining acts. Whoever performs the vow in this way obtains the fruit he desires. ॥55॥
2.4.18.56: Whoever daily, with faith and according to his own ability, performs your worship, O Lord of the gaṇas, for obtaining the fruit of all desires, ॥56॥
2.4.18.57: should worship you, the lord of the gaṇas, with vermilion, sandal paste, rice grains and ketaka flowers, and with many other services. ॥57॥
2.4.18.58: Those who worship you thus with devotion through various services will always have success, and obstacles will be destroyed here. ॥58॥
2.4.18.59: It should be performed by all classes, and especially by women; and by those seeking prosperity, and especially by kings. ॥59॥
2.4.18.60: Whatever one desires, that he surely obtains. Therefore you should always be served by one who has desires. ॥60॥
2.4.18.61: Brahmā said: Thus was it spoken then by Śiva to the great-souled Gaṇeśa. At that time, by the gods and by all the best of sages, ॥61॥
2.4.18.62: having said, so be it, by all of them and by the gaṇas dear to Śambhu, O sage, that lord of the gaṇas was worshipped with the supreme rite. ॥62॥
2.4.18.63: Then all those gaṇas bowed to the lord of the gaṇas and respectfully worshipped him especially with various objects. ॥63॥
2.4.18.64: O lord of sages, the joy that arose in Girijā is indescribable; how could I describe it even with my four mouths? ॥64॥
2.4.18.65: The drums of the gods resounded, the hosts of apsarases danced, the chief gandharvas sang, and a shower of flowers fell. ॥65॥
2.4.18.66: When the lord of the gaṇas was installed, the world then attained well-being; there was a great festival, and all sorrow came to an end. ॥66॥
2.4.18.67: Śivā and Śiva rejoiced exceedingly, O Nārada; there was abundant great auspiciousness everywhere, bestowing happiness. ॥67॥
2.4.18.68: Then all the hosts of gods and likewise the hosts of sages who had assembled there departed by Śiva's command, ॥68॥
2.4.18.69: praising Śivā and Gaṇeśa there again and again, and likewise having extolled Śiva, saying, what a battle that was. ॥69॥
2.4.18.70: When that goddess Girijā became free of anger, Śiva too, approaching Girijā there as before, ॥70॥
2.4.18.71: brought about various joys for the welfare of the worlds — he who, though supreme and delighting in his own Self, is ever ready to accomplish his devotees' purposes. ॥71॥
2.4.18.72: Viṣṇu, having taken leave of Śiva, and I, Brahmā, likewise — we two came to our own abodes after devoutly serving Śiva and Śivā. ॥72॥
2.4.18.73: And you, venerable Nārada, having sung the glory of Śiva and Śivā and taken leave of them, went to your own abode, O lord of sages. ॥73॥
2.4.18.74: All this glory of Śiva and Śivā, blended with the glory of Vighneśa, has been respectfully narrated to you by me, as you asked. ॥74॥
2.4.18.75: Whoever, well-restrained, listens to this most auspicious narrative becomes endowed with every auspiciousness, an abode of auspiciousness. ॥75॥
2.4.18.76: The sonless gains a son, the poor gains wealth, one seeking a wife gains a wife, one seeking offspring gains offspring. ॥76॥
2.4.18.77: The sick gains health, the unfortunate gains good fortune; one regains a lost son or lost wealth, and a woman whose husband is away regains her husband. One overcome by grief becomes free of grief — there is no doubt of this. ॥77॥
2.4.18.78: He in whose house this narrative of Gaṇeśa remains is ever endowed with auspiciousness — there is no doubt of this. ॥78॥
2.4.18.79: Whoever listens to it attentively at the time of setting out on a journey or on a holy day obtains all he desires by the grace of Śrī Gaṇeśa. ॥79॥
2.4.18.iti: Thus ends the eighteenth adhyāya, named Gaṇeśa attains the rank of lord of the gaṇas, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥18॥
2.4.19.1: Nārada said: O dear father, I have heard in full the unsurpassed birth of Gaṇeśa, and also his divine deeds, adorned with great valour. ॥1॥
2.4.19.2: What happened after that, dear father? Tell me the truth, O lord of the gods: the account rich in the glory of Śivā and Śiva, which gives great bliss. ॥2॥
2.4.19.3: Brahmā said: Well asked, O best of sages, by you who are compassionate by nature. Listen with attentive ears; I shall tell it, O best of seers. ॥3॥
2.4.19.4: O chief of brahmins, Śivā and Śiva, watching again and again the play of their two sons, felt the highest, great love for them. ॥4॥
2.4.19.5: As the parents fondled them there, their happiness grew exceedingly; and the two sons always played a great deal with affection and joy. ॥5॥
2.4.19.6: O lord of sages, those two sons, filled with great devotion, rendered service there to their mother and father. ॥6॥
2.4.19.7: And the parents' great affection for Ṣaṇmukha and Gaṇeśa grew ever more, like the moon in the bright fortnight. ॥7॥
2.4.19.8: Once, O divine seer, Śivā and Śiva were sitting there in private, full of love, absorbed in careful deliberation. ॥8॥
2.4.19.9: Śiva and Śivā said: Our two sons have become fit for marriage, so said both of them; how should the auspicious marriage of both our sons be performed? ॥9॥
2.4.19.10: Ṣaṇmukha is most dear, and Gaṇeśa just as much. Thus the two, who delight in play, became agitated with worry. ॥10॥
2.4.19.11: Learning their parents' intention, the two sons too became eager, by that wish, for marriage, O sage. ॥11॥
2.4.19.12: I shall marry first. No, I shall. Again and again, both were constantly engaged in dispute with each other. ॥12॥
2.4.19.13: Hearing their words, the divine couple, lords of the worlds, following worldly custom, were greatly astonished. ॥13॥
2.4.19.14: What should be done? How should the marriage rite of these two be carried out? Having deliberated thus, they devised a wonderful plan. ॥14॥
2.4.19.15: Once, at a suitable time, the parents sat down, called their two sons, and spoke to them there. ॥15॥
2.4.19.16: We have earlier made a rule, which will indeed be pleasing to you two; listen, good sons, we tell you with love exactly how it is. ॥16॥
2.4.19.17: You are both equal, good sons; no distinction is found here. Therefore a fair wager has been set for both sons. ॥17॥
2.4.19.18: Whoever goes round the whole earth and returns first, his auspicious marriage shall be performed first. ॥18॥
2.4.19.19: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of the two, the mighty reed-born Kārttikeya swiftly left the palace to go round the earth. ॥19॥
2.4.19.20: But Gaṇanātha, foremost in intellect, remained right there, reflecting thus again and again in his mind with keen intelligence: ॥20॥
2.4.19.21: What is to be done? Where shall I go? The earth cannot possibly be crossed. Having gone a mere krośa, I could go no further. ॥21॥
2.4.19.22: How much less could I traverse this earth and win happiness thereby? Having reflected thus — hear what Gaṇeśa did. ॥22॥
2.4.19.23: Having bathed in the proper manner and come home himself, he then spoke to his father and mother there. ॥23॥
2.4.19.24: Gaṇeśa said: Two seats have been set here for your worship. Please be seated, dear parents; let my wish be fulfilled. ॥24॥
2.4.19.25: Brahmā said: Hearing his words, Pārvatī and Parameśvara sat on the seats there to receive his worship. ॥25॥
2.4.19.26: Then he worshipped them both and circumambulated them again and again; thus he made seven circuits, and likewise seven prostrations. ॥26॥
2.4.19.27: Then Gaṇeśa, ocean of wisdom, with joined palms, having praised at length his parents who were overcome with love, spoke, dear one. ॥27॥
2.4.19.28: Gaṇeśa said: O mother, O father, hear my excellent words: my splendid marriage must be performed here quickly. ॥28॥
2.4.19.29: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of the great-souled Gaṇeśa, the parents then spoke to him, that treasury of great wisdom. ॥29॥
2.4.19.30: Śiva and Śivā said: You should duly go round the earth with its forests. Kumāra has gone; you too go, and come back first. ॥30॥
2.4.19.31: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of his parents, Gaṇapati, self-controlled yet stirred with anger, promptly spoke there. ॥31॥
2.4.19.32: Gaṇeśa said: O mother, O father, you are regarded as the embodiments of dharma and as wise. O most excellent ones, hear my words properly, in accordance with dharma. ॥32॥
2.4.19.33: I have gone round the earth seven times, again and again. How then can you, my parents, speak thus again here? ॥33॥
2.4.19.34: Brahmā said: Hearing his words then, the parents, performers of great divine play, adopting the worldly way, said to him there: ॥34॥
2.4.19.35: The parents said: When, son, did you traverse the vast earth with its seven continents, bounded by the oceans and filled with great forests? ॥35॥
2.4.19.36: Brahmā said: Hearing these words of Śivā and Śaṅkara, O sage, their son Gaṇeśa, treasury of great wisdom, spoke: ॥36॥
2.4.19.37: Gaṇeśa said: By worshipping you both, Śivā and Śaṅkara, I have, through my own intelligence, made the circuit of the earth bounded by the ocean. ॥37॥
2.4.19.38: Is there not such a statement in the Veda, in the śāstra, or in the compendia of dharma? Is that true, or is it not true? ॥38॥
2.4.19.39: Whoever, having worshipped his parents, performs circumambulation of them, for him the fruit arising from circumambulating the earth certainly comes about. ॥39॥
2.4.19.40: Whoever leaves his parents at home and goes off to a pilgrimage site, his sin is declared to be just like that of killing them. ॥40॥
2.4.19.41: For a son the great holy place is the lotus-feet of his parents; other holy places are attained only after going far away. ॥41॥
2.4.19.42: This holy place is near at hand, easily reached, a means of attaining dharma; for a son and for a wife the holy place at home is most excellent. ॥42॥
2.4.19.43: What the scriptures and Vedas thus declare constantly—would you two now make that false? ॥43॥
2.4.19.44: If this form of yours were to become false here, then the Veda too would become false—there is no doubt. ॥44॥
2.4.19.45: Let my auspicious marriage be performed quickly; or else let the Veda and scriptures be declared false. ॥45॥
2.4.19.46: Whichever of the two is the very best, having considered it properly, that should be done with effort, O parents, embodiments of dharma. ॥46॥
2.4.19.47: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus, Gaṇeśa, son of Pārvatī, of excellent intellect, greatly wise, best of the intelligent, then fell silent. ॥47॥
2.4.19.48: Then that couple, lords of the universe, Pārvatī and Śaṅkara, hearing his words thus, became supremely astonished. ॥48॥
2.4.19.49: Then Śivā and Śiva, praising their son, discerning in intellect and speaking the truth, the two spoke with affection. ॥49॥
2.4.19.50: Śiva and Śivā said: O son, a pure intellect has arisen in you, great-souled one, and the words you have spoken are just so, not otherwise. ॥50॥
2.4.19.51: When sorrow arises, he whose intellect excels—his sorrow perishes, as darkness when the sun is seen. ॥51॥
2.4.19.52: He who has intellect has strength; for the witless, whence strength? A lion maddened with pride was made to fall into a well by a hare. ॥52॥
2.4.19.53: What is declared for a child in the Vedas, scriptures and Purāṇas—all that you have done: the upholding of dharma. ॥53॥
2.4.19.54: What you have done rightly—who else here could do it? It is honoured by us both, and it will not now be done otherwise. ॥54॥
2.4.19.55: Brahmā said: Having spoken thus and reassured Gaṇeśa, the ocean of intellect, the two set their excellent resolve on performing his marriage. ॥55॥
2.4.19.iti: Thus ends the nineteenth adhyāya, named The beginning of the marriage of Gaṇeśa, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥19॥
2.4.20.1: Brahmā said: Meanwhile Prajāpati Viśvarūpa, having considered their undertaking there, felt happy and his mind was pleased. ॥1॥
2.4.20.2: Prajāpati Viśvarūpa had two daughters of divine form, known as Siddhi and Buddhi, auspicious and lovely in every limb. ॥2॥
2.4.20.3: With these two, the lords Girijā and Śaṅkara joyfully had Gaṇeśa's marriage performed as a great festival. ॥3॥
2.4.20.4: All the gods, delighted, came together at that wedding, just as Śiva and Girijā had wished. ॥4॥
2.4.20.5: And so that Viśvakarman performed the marriage accordingly, and the sages and gods obtained supreme joy. ॥5॥
2.4.20.6: Gaṇeśa too then obtained from those two a happiness most hard to attain; O sage, it cannot be described. ॥6॥
2.4.20.7: After some time, two divine sons were born to the great-souled Gaṇeśa from his two wives. ॥7॥
2.4.20.8: To Siddhi, Gaṇeśa's wife, a son named Kṣema was born; to Buddhi was born a most handsome son called Lābha. ॥8॥
2.4.20.9: While the lord of the Gaṇas was thus enjoying inconceivable happiness, the second son then returned, having circled the earth. ॥9॥
2.4.20.10: Just then he was met at home by the great-souled Nārada, who said: I speak what is true, not falsehood, neither with deceit nor out of envy. ॥10॥
2.4.20.11: What your parents, Śivā and Śaṅkara, have done to you, no other in the world would do; I tell you the truth, the truth. ॥11॥
2.4.20.12: Having sent you away, deliberately contriving the pretext of a wrongful circuit, they performed Gaṇeśa's excellent and most splendid marriage. ॥12॥
2.4.20.13: Gaṇeśa, his marriage performed, joyfully obtained two wives, the most excellent jewels among maidens, daughters of Prajāpati Viśvarūpa. ॥13॥
2.4.20.14: He obtained two sons from his two fair-limbed wives: Kṣema from Siddhi and Lābha from Buddhi, bestowers of every happiness. ॥14॥
2.4.20.15: That Gaṇeśa, having obtained two auspicious sons from his two wives, enjoys happiness unceasingly by the will of his mother and father. ॥15॥
2.4.20.16: You traversed the earth with its oceans and forests under the sway of that deceitful command, dear one; and this is the fruit that has come of it. ॥16॥
2.4.20.17: Consider, dear one, the deceit your parents have practised. When one's own masters do such a thing especially, what will others not do? ॥17॥
2.4.20.18: Improper indeed is the act done by those two, your parents. Consider it yourself here; in my mind it is not thought good. ॥18॥
2.4.20.19: If a mother gives poison, if a father sells his child, and the king seizes everything, to whom and what can one say? ॥19॥
2.4.20.20: A wise man who desires peace, dear one, should not look upon the face of one by whom such an extremely harmful deed has been done. ॥20॥
2.4.20.21: Such is the rule of conduct declared in Śruti, in Smṛti and in the śāstras everywhere. I have conveyed it to you today; do as you wish. ॥21॥
2.4.20.22: Brahmā said: Having spoken these words thus to the Kumāra, O Nārada, you, who knew the mind of Maheśvara, fell silent. ॥22॥
2.4.20.23: Skanda too, blazing with the fire of anger, bowed to his father and then went to Mount Krauñca, though restrained by his parents. ॥23॥
2.4.20.24: When we have forbidden you, how can you go today? Though thus prohibited, he said no and went. ॥24॥
2.4.20.25: O parents, I must not stay here even a moment, since such deceit has been practised on me, casting love aside. ॥25॥
2.4.20.26: Having said this he went there, O sage, and he dwells there even today, removing the sins of all people by the mere sight of him. ॥26॥
2.4.20.27: From that day onward, O divine sage, the bachelorhood (kumāratva) of Kārttikeya, Śiva's son, became established. ॥27॥
2.4.20.28: His name is auspicious in the world, renowned in the three worlds, holy, removing all sins, and supremely bestowing celibacy. ॥28॥
2.4.20.29: On the full moon of Kārttika the gods, the sages with the holy places, and the great ascetics always go to see the Kumāra. ॥29॥
2.4.20.30: Whoever has sight of the Lord (Svāmin) on the Kārttika full moon in conjunction with Kṛttikā, all his sin is burnt and he obtains the fruit his heart desires. ॥30॥
2.4.20.31: Umā too fell into grief at separation from Skanda, and wretched, she said to her lord: O lord, go there with me. ॥31॥
2.4.20.32: For her happiness Śambhu himself went to the mountain with a portion of himself; it became the happiness-bringing Jyotirliṅga named Mallikārjuna. ॥32॥
2.4.20.33: Even today Śiva is seen there together with Śivā, fulfiller of the desires of all his devotees, the refuge of the good. ॥33॥
2.4.20.34: The Kumāra, knowing that Śiva had come with Śivā, became averse and was eager to go elsewhere from there. ॥34॥
2.4.20.35: Entreated by the gods and sages, Kārttika moved away three yojanas and stayed at a place at a distance. ॥35॥
2.4.20.36: Śiva and Śivā, anxious with love for their son, go on every festival day to see that Kumāra, O Nārada. ॥36॥
2.4.20.37: On the new-moon day Śambhu himself goes there; on the full-moon day Pārvatī surely goes there. ॥37॥
2.4.20.38: Whatever account of Kārttika and Gaṇeśa you asked about, O lord of sages, I have narrated it in its excellence. ॥38॥
2.4.20.39: A wise man who hears this is freed from all sins and always obtains all his desired, auspicious wishes. ॥39॥
2.4.20.40: Whoever reads or has it read, hears or causes it to be heard, obtains all desires; there is no doubt about this. ॥40॥
2.4.20.41: A brāhmaṇa who hears this becomes endowed with spiritual splendour, a kṣatriya becomes victorious, a vaiśya becomes rich in wealth, and a śūdra attains excellence. ॥41॥
2.4.20.42: A sick man would be freed from disease, one stricken with fear would be freed from fear; a man would not be afflicted by the troubles caused by ghosts, spirits and the like. ॥42॥
2.4.20.43: This narrative is sinless, bestows fame, increases happiness, grants long life, leads to heaven, is incomparable, and brings sons, grandsons and the like. ॥43॥
2.4.20.44: It also bestows liberation and supreme knowledge of Śiva; it brings delight to Śiva and Śivā and increases devotion to Śiva. ॥44॥
2.4.20.45: It should always be listened to by devotees, by the desireless and by those seeking liberation; it grants non-duality with Śiva, is auspicious, and is pervaded by Sadāśiva. ॥45॥
2.4.20.iti: Thus ends the twentieth adhyāya, named The marriage of Gaṇeśa, in the fourth khaṇḍa, the Kumāra-khaṇḍa, of the second saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥20॥
